Depletion rates are either constant or proportional to another stock or the stock itself, forming balancing feedback loops. All numerical constants, such as growth percentages and fixed decrease amounts, are explicitly defined as separate auxiliary variables to maintain model clarity and adherence to best practices.

During operations, we begin with one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current base_stock_xes count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 300% of whatever balacks are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model now incorporates two new stocks, 'whatajigs' and 'balacks', along with their respective inflows and outflows. The 'whatajigs' stock is increased by 'whatajigs additions' which depend on 'base stock x', and decreased by 'whatajigs losses' which depend on 'balacks'. Conversely, the 'balacks' stock is increased by 'balacks benefits' which depend on 'whatajigs', and decreased by 'balacks diminished' which depend on 'base stock y'.

Crucially, a new feedback loop has been closed between 'whatajigs' and 'balacks'. An increase in 'whatajigs' leads to an increase in 'balacks benefits', which in turn increases 'balacks'. This increase in 'balacks' then drives an increase in 'whatajigs losses', ultimately reducing 'whatajigs'. This forms a balancing feedback loop, where the two stocks regulate each other's levels. This structure is reminiscent of a 'Limits to Growth' archetype, where one stock's growth is eventually constrained by another.

To adhere to best practices, all numerical constants in flow equations, both new and existing, have been extracted into dedicated auxiliary variables (e.g., 'output x rate', 'whatajigs addition rate'). This improves model clarity and maintainability.
supportingInfo.title: Interconnected Stocks with Balancing Feedback Loop

A 'crypterals decrease' outflow is added, positively linked to 'existing crypterals' and a 'crypterals decrease rate' constant. This introduces a new cross-system relationship where 'existing posistorathers' influences 'crypterals enhancement', creating a potential coupling between these two inventories. supportingInfo.explanation:
The model has been expanded to include several new interconnected inventories: Whatajigs, Balacks, Whoziewhats, Funkados, and Maxabizers. Each new inventory is modeled as a stock, with associated inflows and outflows that represent growth, gains, losses, reductions, enhancements, additions, and diminishment.

For Whatajigs, a reinforcing loop is created where the stock's growth is dependent on its current size, representing a 'Growth and Underinvestment' archetype if there were limits to growth. A balancing loop is also present due to a constant loss.

Balacks gain from Whatajigs, creating a causal link between these two stocks. Its reduction is linked to existing_store_lambda, establishing a connection to the initial part of the model.

Whoziewhats are enhanced by Balacks, continuing the chain of influence, and also have a self-diminishing balancing loop.

Funkados receive additions from Whoziewhats and are reduced by Maxabizers, creating a dependency between these two new stocks.

Finally, Maxabizers are replenished by Funkados and diminished by existing_store_mu, closing the loop back to another initial stock.

All percentage rates and constant values have been extracted into separate auxiliary variables to adhere to best practices for constant handling, making the model more transparent and easier to modify. The existing flows (replenish_lambda, deplete_lambda, supply_mu) have also been updated to reference these new constant variables.
supportingInfo.title: Interconnected Inventory Dynamics with Feedback Loops

supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures all causal relationships from the background information. The Frimbulators stock starts at 100 and is governed by two flows:

  1. Growth (inflow): A reinforcing loop where the current inventory drives its own growth at a 5% weekly rate. More frimbulators → more growth → even more frimbulators. This is a classic exponential growth structure.

The net behavior depends on the balance between proportional growth and constant removal — at 100 frimbulators, growth equals 5/week and removal equals 5/week, so the system starts in equilibrium. Any perturbation upward triggers the reinforcing growth loop to dominate, while a perturbation downward causes removal to dominate, leading to decline.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures all causal relationships described in the background information as a two-stock system with coupled dynamics.

Whatajigs stock starts at 100 and has two flows:

  • An inflow (whatajigs growth) driven by 5% of its own current level — a self-reinforcing loop.
  • An outflow (whatajigs reduction) driven by 300% of the current balacks count — a cross-stock coupling where balacks deplete whatajigs.

Balacks stock starts at 200 and has two flows:

  • An inflow (balacks growth) driven by 5% of the current whatajigs count — a cross-stock coupling where whatajigs feed balacks.
  • An outflow (balacks reduction) driven by 3% of its own current level — a self-correcting decay loop.

The key feedback structure is a predator-prey-like archetype: whatajigs feed balacks growth (positive cross-link), while balacks drive whatajigs reduction (negative cross-link). Combined with the self-reinforcing growth of whatajigs and the self-correcting decay of balacks, this creates oscillatory or declining dynamics depending on parameter magnitudes. All constants (growth rates, reduction rates) are separated into their own named variables per best practices.

Meanwhile, we begin with one hundred twenty exemintes. Every month, this inventory increases due to exactly eight new exemintes. supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures three inventories and all causal relationships described:

Marticatenes is a stock starting at 50 with a constant inflow of 10/month and a fractional outflow of 20% of its current level. This creates a goal-seeking structure that will converge toward an equilibrium of 50 (where inflow of 10 equals outflow of 20% × 50).

Refluppers is a stock starting at 75 with an inflow driven by 20% of the current marticatenes count. This is the key cross-stock causal link: marticatenes causally influence refluppers through this inflow. The outflow is a constant 8/month. As marticatenes converge to 50, the refluppers inflow converges to 10, and refluppers will seek equilibrium where inflow (10) minus outflow (8) = +2/month, meaning refluppers will grow indefinitely at that point (no balancing feedback on refluppers itself beyond the constant drain).

Exemintes is an independent stock starting at 120 with a constant inflow of 8/month and a fractional outflow of 10%. This is another goal-seeking structure converging toward 80 (where 8 = 10% × 80).

All constants are separated into named variables per best practices. The marticatenes-to-refluppers causal link is the most important cross-system relationship discovered.

Every day, this inventory receives new additions of exactly twelve new dominitoxings. Simultaneously, each day the stock is reduced through 30% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures three interconnected stocks forming a causal chain:

  1. Dominitoxings (initial: 45) receives a constant inflow of 12/day and loses 30% of its current value daily. This creates a goal-seeking structure that will converge to a steady state of 40 (where 12 inflow = 0.3 × 40 outflow).

  2. Povals (initial: 35) is driven by dominitoxings — its inflow equals 30% of the current dominitoxings count. It loses 20% of its own value daily. This creates a dependency where povals tracks dominitoxings behavior with its own decay dynamics.

  3. Auspongs (initial: 90) is driven by povals — its inflow equals 20% of the current povals count. It loses a constant 12/day. This means auspongs' equilibrium depends on where povals settles.

The key causal chain is: dominitoxings → povals → auspongs. Dominitoxings is the upstream driver (independent of the other two), povals depends on dominitoxings, and auspongs depends on povals. Each stock also has its own self-regulating outflow structure. All constants are separated into named variables to maintain model clarity and avoid embedded numerical constants in equations.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In the system, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock loses a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we start the period with seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock has outgoing 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 22% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures three independent-yet-linked inventory systems:

  1. Pablanksills (initial: 110) grow at 6% per quarter (a reinforcing feedback loop — more stock → more growth → more stock) and lose a constant 18 per quarter. The reinforcing growth loop is counteracted by the constant drain.

  2. Posistorathers (initial: 70) receive a constant 25 per quarter and lose 35% of their current level each quarter (a balancing feedback loop — more stock → more outflow → less stock). This structure tends toward an equilibrium around 25/0.35 ≈ 71.4.

  3. Crypterals (initial: 95) receive a constant 18 per quarter plus 35% of the current posistorathers count each quarter. They deplete at 22% per quarter (balancing loop). The key cross-stock causal link is that posistorathers drive an inflow into crypterals — this is the critical inter-system dependency. As posistorathers stabilize, the crypterals inflow from posistorathers also stabilizes, and crypterals will approach their own equilibrium.

All constants (rates and fixed amounts) are extracted into separate named variables to ensure transparency and easy sensitivity analysis. Every cause-and-effect relationship from the original description is explicitly represented.
supportingInfo.title: Three Linked Inventory Growth Depletion Systems

Simultaneously, each week the stock loses a constant three ocs.  Meanwhile, we begin with forty proptimatires. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly five new proptimatires. Simultaneously, each week the stock suffers depletion of 25% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty priaries. Every week, this inventory gains from 10% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 5% of whatever houtals are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate sixty houtals. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly seven new houtals. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 8% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures four interconnected stocks and all causal relationships described:

  1. Proptimatires (initial: 40) has a constant inflow of 5/week and a fractional outflow of 25% of itself per week. This creates a goal-seeking behavior converging toward 20.

  2. Ocs (initial: 25) gains 15% of proptimatires each week (a cross-stock causal link) and loses a constant 3/week. Proptimatires is a key driver of ocs accumulation.

  3. Priaries (initial: 80) gains 10% of proptimatires each week and loses 5% of houtals each week. This stock is uniquely driven by two other stocks — proptimatires drives its inflow and houtals drives its outflow, making it a dependent variable in the system.

  4. Houtals (initial: 60) has a constant inflow of 7/week and a fractional outflow of 8% of itself per week, converging toward 87.5. Houtals indirectly affects priaries through the outflow mechanism.

Key cross-stock causal chains:

  • Proptimatires → ocs: Proptimatires level determines ocs inflow rate
  • Proptimatires → priaries: Proptimatires level determines priaries inflow rate
  • Houtals → priaries: Houtals level determines priaries outflow rate

All constants are separated into named variables per best practices, ensuring no embedded numerical constants in flow equations.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Throughout the process, we have on hand one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory gains from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock gets diminished by 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock suffers depletion of a constant five illigents.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty-five yelbs. Every hour, this inventory benefits from 10% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock is reduced through 12% of whatever trazes are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty-five trazes. Every hour, this inventory gets replenished by exactly fifteen new trazes. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 18% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
The model captures four interconnected stocks and all causal relationships described:

Outrances (initial: 150) has a constant inflow of 20/hour and two fractional outflows (40% and 10% per hour). This creates a goal-seeking/exponential decay structure where the stock will settle toward an equilibrium where inflow equals total outflow.

Illigents (initial: 30) receives an inflow driven by 40% of the current Outrances level — this is a key cross-stock causal link where Outrances causes Illigents to grow. It loses a constant 5 illigents/hour.

Yelbs (initial: 65) receives an inflow driven by 10% of Outrances — another cross-stock causal link. Its outflow is driven by 12% of the current Trazes level, creating a second cross-stock causal link where Trazes causes Yelbs to decline.

Trazes (initial: 85) has a constant inflow of 15/hour and a fractional outflow of 18% per hour, forming an independent goal-seeking structure.

The critical cross-stock causal chains are:

  • Outrances → Illigents: Outrances level drives illigents inflow
  • Outrances → Yelbs: Outrances level drives yelbs inflow
  • Trazes → Yelbs: Trazes level drives yelbs outflow

All constants are separated into named variables per best practices. Each stock has balancing feedback through its fractional outflows, representing natural decay or depletion processes.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: At the facility, our records indicate one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock decreases by a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory grows through incoming 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory gains from 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock suffers depletion of 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we start the period with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of whatever whoziewhats are currently available.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures five interconnected inventory stocks and all their causal relationships:

  1. Whatajigs (initial: 100) has a self-reinforcing growth loop — its inflow is 5% of itself (positive feedback) — and a constant outflow of 3 per year.

  2. Balacks (initial: 200) receives inflow driven by whatajigs (5% of whatajigs) and loses 3% of its own stock each year. This creates a causal chain from whatajigs → balacks.

  3. Whoziewhats (initial: 200) receives inflow driven by balacks (5% of balacks) and loses 3% of its own stock. This extends the chain: whatajigs → balacks → whoziewhats.

  4. Funkados (initial: 12) receives inflow from whoziewhats (5% of whoziewhats) but its outflow is uniquely driven by maxabizers (3% of maxabizers), creating a cross-stock dependency.

  5. Maxabizers (initial: 88) receives inflow from funkados (5% of funkados) but its outflow is driven by whoziewhats (3% of whoziewhats), creating another cross-stock dependency.

The last two stocks form an interesting coupled system: funkados and maxabizers each influence the other's flows, while both are also influenced by whoziewhats. This creates feedback loops between funkados and maxabizers — specifically, maxabizers depletes funkados while funkados feeds maxabizers, forming a balancing dynamic. Meanwhile, whoziewhats acts as an external driver affecting both the funkados inflow and the maxabizers outflow.

All constants (growth rates, loss rates, fractions) are separated into named variables to maintain model clarity and enable sensitivity analysis.
supportingInfo.title: Five Coupled Inventory Stocks Causal Model

During operations, we begin with one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current base_stock_xes count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 300% of whatever balacks are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added four new stocks and their associated flows and constants to the existing model, preserving all original variable names.

Whatajigs (initial value 100) accumulates via whatajig_additions (5% of base_stock_x per year) and depletes via whatajig_losses (300% of balacks per year). Balacks (initial value 200) accumulates via balack_additions (5% of whatajigs per year) and depletes via balack_losses (3% of base_stock_y per year).

This creates a critical cross-coupling feedback loop between whatajigs and balacks: more whatajigs → more balack additions → more balacks → more whatajig losses → fewer whatajigs. This is a balancing loop — as whatajigs grow, they feed balacks, which in turn drain whatajigs back down. The loop structure resembles a predator-prey archetype where balacks act as a drain on whatajigs while whatajigs feed balacks.

All numerical constants (fractions like 0.05, 3.0, 0.03) were extracted into named auxiliary variables to follow best practices and avoid embedding constants directly in flow equations. The existing model variables (base_stock_x, base_stock_y, input_x, output_x, input_y) were left unchanged except that output_x now references a named constant output_x_fraction and input_y now references input_y_fraction.

testParams.prompt:
Please add the following to my model...
In our organization, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gains from 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we have on hand seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock decreases by 22% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added three new stock-and-flow structures to the existing model while preserving all original variables unchanged:

Pablanksills — A stock initialized at 110 with a reinforcing growth loop (R): 6% of its current level feeds back as growth each quarter, while a constant 18 units are depleted. The reinforcing loop (pablanksills → pablanksills_growth → pablanksills) drives exponential growth, counterbalanced by constant depletion.

Posistorathers — A stock initialized at 70 with a constant inflow of 25 per quarter and a balancing loop (B): 35% of the current stock is depleted each quarter. This goal-seeking structure will converge toward an equilibrium where inflow equals outflow (approximately 71.4 units).

Crypterals — A stock initialized at 95 with two inflows and one outflow. It receives a constant 18 per quarter plus an enhancement equal to 35% of the current posistorathers count. It loses 22% of its own level each quarter (balancing loop). The cross-stock link from posistorathers to crypterals_enhancement is a key causal discovery: posistorathers drives crypteral accumulation. As posistorathers stabilizes near its equilibrium, the enhancement flow stabilizes too, and crypterals will seek its own equilibrium.

All constants were extracted into named auxiliary variables to follow best practices. I also properly parameterized the pre-existing refill_epsilon, leak_epsilon, and pump_zeta equations with named constants (refill_epsilon_fraction, leak_epsilon_constant, pump_zeta_constant) that were previously embedded as numbers.
supportingInfo.title: Three New Inventories With Cross Stock Link

In our organization, we begin with twenty-five ocs. Every week, this inventory increases due to 15% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock has outgoing 4% of whatever existing_chamber_etas are currently available.  Meanwhile, we have on hand forty proptimatires. Every week, this inventory receives new additions of 9% of the current existing_chamber_thetas count. Simultaneously, each week the stock has outgoing 25% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with eighty priaries. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by 10% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 5% of whatever houtals are currently available.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty houtals. Every week, this inventory increases due to exactly seven new houtals. Simultaneously, each week the stock suffers depletion of 8% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added four new stocks with their associated flows and constants as described:

  1. ocs (initial value 25): Inflow driven by 15% of proptimatires, outflow driven by 4% of existing_chamber_eta. This creates a cross-stock dependency where proptimatires feeds ocs growth and existing_chamber_eta drives ocs depletion.

  2. proptimatires (initial value 40): Inflow driven by 9% of existing_chamber_theta, outflow is 25% of its own level (a first-order decay). This connects existing_chamber_theta to the broader system since proptimatires also drives ocs_inflow and priaries_inflow.

  3. priaries (initial value 80): Inflow driven by 10% of proptimatires, outflow driven by 5% of houtals. This creates another cross-stock dependency linking proptimatires and houtals to priaries dynamics.

  4. houtals (initial value 60): Inflow is a constant 7 units/week, outflow is 8% of its own level (first-order decay). Houtals also influences priaries through the priaries outflow.

Key causal chains identified: existing_chamber_theta → proptimatires → ocs (and proptimatires → priaries), existing_chamber_eta → ocs outflow, and houtals → priaries outflow. All constants were extracted into separate named variables following best practices. The existing_chamber_eta self-reinforcing loop (positive feedback through injection_eta) remains intact from the original model.

Please add the following to my model...
In my business, the baseline inventory shows one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock has outgoing 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock is reduced through 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock decreases by a constant five illigents.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty-five yelbs. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of 10% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 12% of whatever trazes are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty-five trazes. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of exactly fifteen new trazes. Simultaneously, each hour the stock experiences losses of 18% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added four new inventory stocks and their associated flows and constants to the existing model:

  1. Outrances Inventory (initial: 150) — gains a constant 20/hour, loses 40% and 10% of its current level each hour through two separate outflows. The two fractional outflows create a goal-seeking/draining dynamic where the stock will settle toward an equilibrium where inflow equals total outflow (20 = 0.5 × stock, so equilibrium at 40 outrances).

  2. Illigents Inventory (initial: 30) — gains 40% of the current outrances count each hour and loses a constant 5/hour. This creates a cross-stock dependency where outrances drives illigents accumulation. As outrances declines toward equilibrium, the illigents inflow will also decline.

  3. Yelbs Inventory (initial: 65) — gains 10% of current outrances each hour and loses 12% of current trazes each hour. This is notable because the outflow depends on a different stock (trazes), creating an interesting cross-stock coupling where yelbs depletion is governed by trazes levels rather than its own.

  4. Trazes Inventory (initial: 85) — gains a constant 15/hour and loses 18% of its current amount each hour. This is a classic goal-seeking structure that will converge to equilibrium at approximately 83.3 trazes.

All constants were extracted into separate named variables following best practices. The outrances stock serves as a hub connecting to both illigents and yelbs through their inflows, while trazes independently influences yelbs through its outflow.

testParams.prompt:
Please add the following to my model...
In my business, we start the period with one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory is enhanced by 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock loses a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, we begin with two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory gains from 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock is reduced through 3% of whatever existing_store_lambdas are currently available.  Meanwhile, we have on hand two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory is enhanced by 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock is reduced through 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we begin with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of whatever existing_store_mus are currently available.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added five new inventory chains to the existing model while preserving all original variables unchanged.

Whatajigs is a stock starting at 100 with a reinforcing growth loop (5% of itself per year) and a constant drain of 3 per year. The self-referential growth creates a classic reinforcing (R) loop.

Balacks starts at 200 and is driven by a cross-stock inflow (5% of whatajigs) and a cross-stock outflow (3% of existing_store_lambda). This creates causal chains linking whatajigs → balacks and existing_store_lambda → balacks.

Whoziewhats starts at 200 with inflow from 5% of balacks and outflow of 3% of itself. The self-referential outflow creates a balancing (B) loop, while the balacks dependency chains back through whatajigs.

Funkados starts at 12 with inflow from 5% of whoziewhats and outflow from 3% of maxabizers. This creates a critical cross-link to maxabizers.

Maxabizers starts at 88 with inflow from 5% of funkados and outflow from 3% of existing_store_mu. The funkados↔maxabizers pair forms a feedback structure: funkados gains drive maxabizers gains, while maxabizers levels drive funkados losses — creating a coupled balancing loop between the two stocks.

All constants were extracted into named variables per best practices. Each flow depends on clearly identified stocks and fractional parameters, ensuring full traceability of every cause-and-effect relationship.
supportingInfo.title: Five Linked Inventory Chains With Feedback

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures a coupled two-stock system with interesting dynamics. Whatajigs starts at 100 and experiences self-reinforcing growth (5% annually) while being depleted by balacks at a high rate (3 whatajigs removed per balack per year). Balacks starts at 200 and grows based on whatajigs (5% of whatajigs count annually) while experiencing natural decay (3% annually).

The system exhibits a predator-prey-like archetype where balacks act as a drain on whatajigs, but whatajigs fuel balacks growth. Given the high reduction rate (300%), the initial 200 balacks will rapidly deplete whatajigs, which will then reduce balacks growth, eventually causing balacks to decline through decay. This creates a collapse dynamic rather than oscillation due to the asymmetric coupling strengths.
supportingInfo.title: Coupled Inventory System with Predator Prey Dynamics

Exemintes System: An independent stock starting at 120 units with constant inflow of 8 per month and proportional outflow of 10% of current inventory.

The critical causal discovery finding is the inter-system relationship: marticatenes directly causes changes in refluppers inflow, creating a one-way coupling between these inventories. All constants are separated into named variables to maintain proper model structure.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In our organization, the baseline inventory shows thirty-five povals. Every day, this inventory benefits from 30% of the current dominitoxings count. Simultaneously, each day the stock gets diminished by 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand ninety auspongs. Every day, this inventory gains from 20% of the current povals count. Simultaneously, each day the stock experiences losses of a constant twelve auspongs.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows forty-five dominitoxings. Every day, this inventory receives new additions of exactly twelve new dominitoxings. Simultaneously, each day the stock is reduced through 30% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures three interconnected inventory systems with distinct dynamics:

Dominitoxings operates as a source stock that receives constant additions (12/day) while losing 30% of its current level daily. This creates goal-seeking behavior toward an equilibrium of 40 units.

Povals depends on dominitoxings - its inflow equals 30% of the dominitoxings count. It simultaneously loses 20% of itself daily. This creates a cascading dependency where povals behavior follows dominitoxings dynamics.

Auspongs sits at the end of the causal chain, receiving 20% of povals as inflow while losing a constant 12 units daily. The constant outflow (rather than proportional) means auspongs could potentially go negative if povals drops too low.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In the system, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock loses a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we start the period with seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock has outgoing 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 22% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures three independent inventory systems with one cross-system causal link.

Pablanksills exhibits a reinforcing growth loop where the stock feeds back into its own growth (6% per quarter), balanced by a constant drain of 18 units per quarter. This creates goal-seeking behavior where the stock will stabilize when growth equals loss.

Posistorathers follows the opposite pattern: constant inflow of 25 units per quarter with proportional outflow (35% per quarter). This also creates goal-seeking dynamics toward an equilibrium.

Crypterals has the most complex structure with two inflows—a constant 18 units per quarter plus a contribution equal to 35% of current posistorathers—and proportional depletion at 22% per quarter. The key cross-system causal relationship is that posistorathers directly influences crypterals growth, creating a one-way dependency between these two subsystems.

All constants are explicitly named as separate variables to maintain model clarity and enable sensitivity analysis.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In the system, our records indicate twenty-five ocs. Every week, this inventory receives new additions of 15% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock loses a constant three ocs.  Meanwhile, we begin with forty proptimatires. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly five new proptimatires. Simultaneously, each week the stock suffers depletion of 25% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty priaries. Every week, this inventory gains from 10% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 5% of whatever houtals are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate sixty houtals. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly seven new houtals. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 8% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
This model captures four interconnected inventory systems with all causal relationships extracted:

Ocs Stock: Starts at 25, gains from 15% of proptimatires weekly, loses a constant 3 per week. This creates a cross-stock dependency where proptimatires drives ocs accumulation.

Proptimatires Stock: Starts at 40, gains a constant 5 per week, loses 25% of itself weekly. This is a classic goal-seeking structure that will stabilize around 20 units (where inflow equals outflow).

Priaries Stock: Starts at 80, gains from 10% of proptimatires weekly, loses based on 5% of houtals. This stock has two cross-dependencies: its inflow depends on proptimatires, and its outflow depends on houtals.

Houtals Stock: Starts at 60, gains a constant 7 per week, loses 8% of itself weekly. Similar goal-seeking behavior, stabilizing around 87.5 units.

The key cross-stock causal chains are: proptimatires → ocs inflow → ocs, proptimatires → priaries inflow → priaries, and houtals → priaries outflow → priaries. Each stock also has self-regulating feedback through fractional outflows.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Throughout the process, we have on hand one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory gains from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock gets diminished by 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. supportingInfo.explanation:

Outrances starts at 150 and has a constant inflow of 20 per hour, with two separate percentage-based outflows (40% and 10% of current stock). This creates balancing feedback loops where higher stock levels drive higher outflows.

Illigents starts at 30 and receives inflow equal to 40% of current outrances, creating a cross-stock causal link where outrances drive illigents growth. It depletes at a constant 5 per hour.

Yelbs starts at 65 and receives inflow equal to 10% of current outrances (another cross-stock link). Uniquely, its outflow depends on trazes (12% of trazes), creating a causal relationship where trazes levels affect yelbs depletion.

Trazes starts at 85 with constant inflow of 15 per hour and depletes at 18% of current stock, following a standard decay pattern.

The key cross-system causal relationships are: outrances → illigents inflow, outrances → yelbs inflow, and trazes → yelbs outflow.

testParams.prompt: Please give me a model which includes all causal relationships in the background information.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: At the facility, our records indicate one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock decreases by a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory grows through incoming 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory gains from 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock suffers depletion of 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we start the period with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of whatever whoziewhats are currently available.

supportingInfo.explanation: This model captures a cascading inventory system with five interconnected stocks. Whatajigs operates as a self-reinforcing stock with 5% growth based on its own level, balanced by a constant 3-unit annual decrease. Balacks receives inflows driven by whatajigs (5% of whatajigs count) while experiencing proportional decay (3% of its own level). Whoziewhats follows a similar pattern, growing from balacks and decaying proportionally. The system becomes more complex with funkados and maxabizers, which form a coupled subsystem: funkados grows from whoziewhats but decreases based on maxabizers, while maxabizers grows from funkados but decreases based on whoziewhats. This creates cross-dependencies where whoziewhats influences both the growth of funkados and the decrease of maxabizers, and maxabizers influences the decrease of funkados. The causal chain flows from whatajigs through balacks to whoziewhats, then branches into the funkados-maxabizers coupled system with feedback effects.
supportingInfo.title: Cascading Inventory System with Cross Dependencies

supportingInfo.explanation: The model now captures two key feedback dynamics. During operations, we begin with one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current base_stock_xes count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 300% of whatever balacks are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added two new inventory stocks to the model: whatajigs (starting at 100 units) and balacks (starting at 200 units). These two stocks form an interconnected system with the existing base stocks.

Whatajigs dynamics:

  • Gains additions at 5% of base_stock_x annually
  • Loses inventory at 300% of current balacks count annually

Balacks dynamics:

  • Gains additions at 5% of current whatajigs count annually
  • Loses inventory at 3% of base_stock_y annually

This creates a balancing feedback loop between whatajigs and balacks: as whatajigs increase, they drive up balacks additions, but more balacks then accelerate whatajigs losses. This interdependency means the two inventories will tend toward equilibrium states determined by the external influences from base_stock_x and base_stock_y.
supportingInfo.title: Interconnected Inventory System with Feedback Dynamics

testParams.prompt:
Please add the following to my model...
At the warehouse, our records indicate fifty marticatenes. Every month, this inventory is enhanced by 15% of the current existing_pool_alphas count. Simultaneously, each month the stock has outgoing 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand seventy-five refluppers. Every month, this inventory benefits from 20% of the current marticatenes count. Simultaneously, each month the stock decreases by 10% of whatever existing_pool_betas are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate one hundred twenty exemintes. Every month, this inventory benefits from exactly eight new exemintes. Simultaneously, each month the stock suffers depletion of 10% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added three new inventory stocks to the warehouse system:

Marticatenes starts at 50 units and has a reinforcing relationship with existing_pool_alpha. Each month, 15% of existing_pool_alpha flows in, while 20% of the current marticatenes stock flows out. This creates a balancing loop on the outflow side.

Refluppers starts at 75 units and connects two parts of the system. Its inflow depends on marticatenes (20% monthly), creating a chain from existing_pool_alpha through marticatenes to refluppers. Uniquely, its outflow depends on existing_pool_beta (10% monthly), creating a cross-system dependency.

Exemintes starts at 120 units and operates independently with a constant inflow of 8 units per month and a proportional outflow of 10% of its current level. This creates a goal-seeking behavior toward an equilibrium of 80 units.

All numerical constants were extracted into separate named variables following best practices for model transparency and sensitivity analysis.
supportingInfo.title: Three Warehouse Inventories with Cross Dependencies

Please add the following to my model...
In our organization, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gains from 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we have on hand seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock decreases by 22% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation: I added three new inventory systems to the model. Pablanksills starts at 110 units with a reinforcing growth loop (6% of current stock) counterbalanced by constant depletion of 18 units per quarter. Posistorathers begins at 70 units, receiving constant additions of 25 per quarter while experiencing proportional depletion at 35% of current stock—this creates a balancing structure that will stabilize around an equilibrium. Crypterals starts at 95 units with two inflows: constant replenishment of 18 per quarter plus enhancement driven by 35% of the posistorathers count, creating a cross-stock dependency. Crypterals decrease at 22% of current stock per quarter. The posistorathers-to-crypterals link represents an important causal connection where the level of one inventory directly influences the growth of another, demonstrating how separate subsystems can be coupled through shared dependencies.

testParams.prompt:
Please add the following to my model...
In my business, the baseline inventory shows one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock has outgoing 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock is reduced through 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock decreases by a constant five illigents.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty-five yelbs. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of 10% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 12% of whatever trazes are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty-five trazes. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of exactly fifteen new trazes. Simultaneously, each hour the stock experiences losses of 18% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added four interconnected inventory systems to the existing model:

  1. Baseline Inventory Outrances: A stock starting at 150 with constant inflow of 20 per hour and two percentage-based outflows (40% outgoing and 10% reduction). This creates a draining dynamic where outflows exceed inflows at higher stock levels.

  2. Illigents Inventory: Starting at 30, this stock gains from outrances (40% of current outrances per hour) and loses a constant 5 per hour. This creates a causal link where outrances drive illigent accumulation.

  3. Yelbs Inventory: Starting at 65, this stock receives 10% of current outrances per hour but loses based on trazes inventory (12% of trazes per hour). This creates an interesting cross-dependency where one inventory's level affects another's outflow.

  4. Trazes Inventory: Starting at 85 with constant inflow of 15 per hour and 18% loss rate. Trazes influence yelb losses, creating a causal chain.

The key causal discoveries include: outrances driving both illigent gains and yelb additions, and trazes driving yelb losses. All rate constants are separated into named variables following best practices.
supportingInfo.title: Four Interconnected Inventory Systems with Cross Dependencies

testParams.prompt:
Please add the following to my model...
In my business, we start the period with one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory is enhanced by 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock loses a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, we begin with two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory gains from 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock is reduced through 3% of whatever existing_store_lambdas are currently available.  Meanwhile, we have on hand two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory is enhanced by 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory receives new additions of 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock is reduced through 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we begin with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of whatever existing_store_mus are currently available.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
I added five interconnected inventory systems to the existing model:

  1. Whatajigs - A self-reinforcing stock starting at 100 units with 5% growth (reinforcing loop) and constant 3-unit annual loss.

  2. Balacks - Starting at 200 units, this stock gains from whatajigs (5% of whatajigs count) creating a cross-stock dependency, while losing based on existing_store_lambda (3% of lambda), linking the new system to the original model.

  3. Whoziewhats - Starting at 200 units with gains from balacks (5%) and self-diminishment (3% of its own level), creating a balancing feedback on itself.

  4. Funkados - Starting at 12 units, gains from whoziewhats (5%) but loses based on maxabizers (3%), creating a cross-dependency.

  5. Maxabizers - Starting at 88 units, replenished from funkados (5%) and diminished based on existing_store_mu (3%), connecting back to the original model.

This creates a chain of dependencies: whatajigs → balacks → whoziewhats → funkados ↔ maxabizers, with the original stocks (existing_store_lambda and existing_store_mu) influencing balacks and maxabizers respectively. The funkados-maxabizers relationship forms a balancing loop where each stock's outflow depends on the other.
supportingInfo.title: Five Interconnected Inventory Chains with Cross-Dependencies

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: At the facility, we have on hand twenty frimbulators. Every day, this inventory increases due to 2% growth relative to its current size.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures the exponential growth archetype described in the background information. The key causal relationships are:

  1. Frimbulators → Growth (+): The current inventory drives the absolute amount of daily growth (reinforcing loop).
  2. Growth Rate → Growth (+): The 2% daily rate scales the growth flow.
  3. Growth → Frimbulators (+): Growth is an inflow that accumulates into the stock.

The reinforcing (positive feedback) loop between Frimbulators and Growth produces classic exponential growth: as inventory increases, the absolute daily addition also increases, which further increases inventory. The Growth Rate constant (0.02 per day) is kept as a separate named variable per best practices, avoiding embedded constants in equations.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In our organization, there are initially one hundred frimbulators. Every week, this inventory grows through incoming 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each week the stock decreases by a constant five frimbulators.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures the two causal mechanisms described:

  1. Reinforcing loop (Growth): The Frimbulators stock drives the Growth flow via the Growth Rate (5% per week). This creates a reinforcing (positive feedback) loop — more frimbulators produce more growth, which adds more frimbulators.

  2. Draining flow (Constant Decrease): A fixed Decrease Amount of 5 frimbulators per week is subtracted from the stock each week, independent of the stock level. This is a simple open-loop drain.

All causal relationships are explicitly represented:

  • Frimbulators → Growth (stock size drives proportional inflow)
  • Growth Rate → Growth (rate parameter scales the inflow)
  • Growth → Frimbulators (inflow adds to stock)
  • Decrease Amount → Constant Decrease (constant parameter drives outflow)
  • Constant Decrease → Frimbulators (outflow drains stock)

Starting at 100 frimbulators, the reinforcing growth (5%) exactly offsets the constant drain (5 units/week) at the initial condition, but as the stock grows the growth flow will exceed the drain, producing net growth over time.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures two interacting stocks — Whatajigs and Balacks — with four flows governing their dynamics, reflecting all causal relationships described in the background information.

Stocks

  • Whatajigs starts at 100 units and is driven by two flows: a self-reinforcing growth (5% of itself) and a predatory reduction (300% of Balacks).
  • Balacks starts at 200 units and is driven by two flows: a growth term fed by Whatajigs (5% of Whatajigs) and a self-decay (3% of itself).

Causal Structure

The model contains two reinforcing loops and two balancing loops:

  1. Reinforcing loop (Whatajigs): More Whatajigs → more Whatajigs Growth → more Whatajigs.
  2. Balancing loop (Whatajigs-Balacks predation): More Balacks → more Whatajigs Reduction → fewer Whatajigs → less Balacks Growth → fewer Balacks.
  3. Reinforcing loop (Balacks via Whatajigs): More Whatajigs → more Balacks Growth → more Balacks.
  4. Balancing loop (Balacks decay): More Balacks → more Balacks Reduction → fewer Balacks.

All numerical constants (growth and reduction rates) are represented as separate named variables to maintain clean equation structure and full causal traceability.
supportingInfo.title: Whatajigs and Balacks Predator-Prey Dynamics

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: During operations, we begin with fifty marticatenes. Every month, this inventory gains from exactly ten new marticatenes. Simultaneously, each month the stock is reduced through 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand seventy-five refluppers. Every month, this inventory is enhanced by 20% of the current marticatenes count. Simultaneously, each month the stock loses a constant eight refluppers.  Meanwhile, we begin with one hundred twenty exemintes. Every month, this inventory increases due to exactly eight new exemintes. Simultaneously, each month the stock is reduced through 10% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures three independent stock-and-flow structures with all causal relationships made explicit for causal discovery purposes.

Marticatenes

A balancing loop governs this stock: the outflow is 20% of the current stock, which means as the stock grows the outflow grows, pushing the stock back toward an equilibrium. A constant inflow of 10 units/month offsets this drain. The equilibrium level is where inflow equals outflow: 10 = 0.2 × Marticatenes, so equilibrium ≈ 50 units.

Refluppers

This stock is driven externally by the marticatenes stock — its inflow is 20% of the current marticatenes level, creating a cross-stock causal link. A constant outflow of 8 units/month drains it. This is an open-loop structure where refluppers depend on marticatenes dynamics.

Exemintes

Another balancing loop: the outflow is 10% of the current stock, with a constant inflow of 8 units/month. Equilibrium ≈ 80 units (8 = 0.1 × Exemintes).

All constants (inflow rates, drain rates, outflow rates) are represented as explicit named variables to fully expose every causal link for causal discovery.
supportingInfo.title: Three Stock Causal Discovery System Dynamics Model

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In our organization, the baseline inventory shows thirty-five povals. Every day, this inventory benefits from 30% of the current dominitoxings count. Simultaneously, each day the stock gets diminished by 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand ninety auspongs. Every day, this inventory gains from 20% of the current povals count. Simultaneously, each day the stock experiences losses of a constant twelve auspongs.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows forty-five dominitoxings. Every day, this inventory receives new additions of exactly twelve new dominitoxings. Simultaneously, each day the stock is reduced through 30% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures three interconnected stocks with their respective flows and rate constants, designed to expose every causal relationship described in the background information.

Three Stocks

  • Povals (initial: 35): Gains from 30% of Dominitoxings daily; loses 20% of itself daily. This creates a balancing loop (Povals → Povals Outflow → Povals) and a cross-stock driver (Dominitoxings → Povals Inflow → Povals).
  • Auspongs (initial: 90): Gains from 20% of Povals daily; loses a constant 12 units daily. This creates another cross-stock driver (Povals → Auspongs Inflow → Auspongs) and a drain loop with a fixed outflow.
  • Dominitoxings (initial: 45): Gains a constant 12 units daily; loses 30% of itself daily. This creates a balancing loop (Dominitoxings → Dominitoxings Outflow → Dominitoxings) with a fixed inflow driving it toward equilibrium.

Causal Chain

All rate constants (0.3, 0.2, 0.3) and fixed values (12, 12) are represented as separate named variables to make every causal driver explicit and traceable, supporting the causal discovery objective. The chain runs: Dominitoxings → Povals → Auspongs, with each stock also governed by its own internal balancing feedback.
supportingInfo.title: Three Interconnected Inventory Stocks Causal Discovery

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In the system, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock loses a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we start the period with seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock has outgoing 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, the baseline inventory shows ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 22% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures three independent stock-and-flow structures with one cross-stock causal link:

Pablanksills (Reinforcing + Drain)

  • A reinforcing loop: the stock grows at 6% of its current size (endogenous growth), creating a positive feedback loop between the stock and its growth flow.
  • A constant drain of 18 units per quarter acts as a fixed outflow, independent of stock size.
  • The net behavior depends on whether the 6% growth exceeds the constant 18-unit loss.

Posistorathers (Constant Inflow + Fractional Outflow)

  • A constant inflow of 25 units per quarter replenishes the stock.
  • A balancing loop: 35% of the current stock leaves each quarter, creating a goal-seeking structure that drives the stock toward an equilibrium (25 / 0.35 ≈ 71.4 posistorathers).

Crypterals (Dual Inflow + Fractional Outflow)

  • A constant inflow of 18 units per quarter.
  • A cross-stock causal link: 35% of the current Posistorathers stock flows into Crypterals each quarter, making Posistorathers a driver of Crypterals accumulation.
  • A balancing loop: 22% of the current Crypterals stock is depleted each quarter.
  • All three rate constants and the posistorathers fraction are represented as explicit named variables to fully expose every causal relationship for causal discovery purposes.
supportingInfo.title: Three Stock Causal Discovery System Dynamics Model

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: In the system, our records indicate twenty-five ocs. Every week, this inventory receives new additions of 15% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock loses a constant three ocs.  Meanwhile, we begin with forty proptimatires. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly five new proptimatires. Simultaneously, each week the stock suffers depletion of 25% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty priaries. Every week, this inventory gains from 10% of the current proptimatires count. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 5% of whatever houtals are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate sixty houtals. Every week, this inventory is enhanced by exactly seven new houtals. Simultaneously, each week the stock gets diminished by 8% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures four interacting stocks — ocs, proptimatires, priaries, and houtals — each with their own inflows and outflows, plus cross-stock causal links.

Ocs

Starts at 25. Its inflow is driven by 15% of the current proptimatires level (a positive cross-stock link), and its outflow is a fixed constant of 3 per week. This creates a reinforcing dependency on proptimatires.

Proptimatires

Starts at 40. Its inflow is a fixed constant of 5 per week, and its outflow is a balancing loop — 25% of its own current level drains it each week. This self-regulating structure drives proptimatires toward an equilibrium of 20 (5 / 0.25).

Priaries

Starts at 80. Its inflow is driven by 10% of proptimatires (positive cross-stock link from proptimatires), and its outflow is driven by 5% of houtals (a negative cross-stock pressure from houtals). This creates an interesting dynamic where proptimatires feeds priaries while houtals depletes it.

Houtals

Starts at 60. Its inflow is a fixed constant of 7 per week, and its outflow is a balancing loop — 8% of its own current level drains it each week. This drives houtals toward an equilibrium of 87.5 (7 / 0.08). As houtals grows toward equilibrium, it increasingly drains priaries.

All numerical constants are represented as separate named variables to maintain clean equation structure. Every causal relationship described in the background information is explicitly captured in both the flow equations and the relationships list.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Throughout the process, we have on hand one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory gains from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock gets diminished by 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we start the period with thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock suffers depletion of a constant five illigents.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty-five yelbs. Every hour, this inventory benefits from 10% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock is reduced through 12% of whatever trazes are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty-five trazes. Every hour, this inventory gets replenished by exactly fifteen new trazes. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 18% of its current amount.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures four interacting stocks with their respective inflows and outflows, and all causal relationships described in the background information.

Outrances

A stock starting at 150 with a fixed inflow of 20 per hour and two fractional outflows: 40% and 10% of the current stock per hour. Both outflows form balancing (negative feedback) loops with the outrances stock — as outrances grow, outflows grow, restraining further growth.

Illigents

A stock starting at 30 driven by outrances as a source: 40% of current outrances flows in each hour. A constant outflow of 5 per hour depletes it. Outrances causally drives the illigents inflow (positive polarity).

Yelbs

A stock starting at 65 also fed by outrances (10% per hour). Its outflow is driven by trazes (12% of current trazes per hour), creating a cross-stock causal link from trazes to yelbs.

Trazes

A stock starting at 85 with a fixed inflow of 15 per hour and a fractional outflow of 18% of current trazes per hour, forming a balancing loop. Trazes also causally drives the yelbs outflow.

All constants are represented as separate named variables to maintain clean equation structure and full causal traceability.

testParams.prompt: Please give me a model which includes all causal relationships in the background information.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: At the facility, our records indicate one hundred whatajigs. Every year, this inventory gets replenished by 5% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each year the stock decreases by a constant three whatajigs.  Meanwhile, our records indicate two hundred balacks. Every year, this inventory grows through incoming 5% of the current whatajigs count. Simultaneously, each year the stock gets diminished by 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand two hundred whoziewhats. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current balacks count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, there are initially twelve funkados. Every year, this inventory gains from 5% of the current whoziewhats count. Simultaneously, each year the stock suffers depletion of 3% of whatever maxabizers are currently available.  Meanwhile, we start the period with eighty-eight maxabizers. Every year, this inventory increases due to 5% of the current funkados count. Simultaneously, each year the stock experiences losses of 3% of whatever whoziewhats are currently available.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Structure

This model captures a cascade of five interconnected stocks — Whatajigs, Balacks, Whoziewhats, Funkados, and Maxabizers — each with its own inflow and outflow, forming a chain of causal dependencies.

Whatajigs

A reinforcing loop drives Whatajigs growth (5% of itself), while a constant drain of 3 units per year acts as a fixed outflow. This is a classic exponential growth with linear drain structure.

Balacks

Balacks receives inflows from Whatajigs (5% of Whatajigs) and loses 3% of its own stock. This creates a cross-stock dependency where Whatajigs drives Balacks growth, while Balacks self-regulates its own loss — a balancing loop on the loss side.

Whoziewhats

Whoziewhats mirrors the Balacks structure: it grows at 5% of Balacks and loses 3% of itself. This continues the cascade chain from Whatajigs → Balacks → Whoziewhats.

Funkados

Funkados introduces a cross-stock coupling: it grows at 5% of Whoziewhats but loses 3% of Maxabizers (not itself). This creates a cross-stock drain where Maxabizers deplete Funkados.

Maxabizers

Maxabizers grows at 5% of Funkados and loses 3% of Whoziewhats. This creates a feedback loop back into the chain: Whoziewhats → Maxabizers Loss, and Funkados → Maxabizers Growth, while Maxabizers → Funkados Loss. This forms a mutual inhibition structure between Funkados and Maxabizers, mediated by Whoziewhats.

All rate constants are represented as explicit named variables to maintain clean equation structure and support causal discovery.
supportingInfo.title: Five Stock Cascade with Cross-Stock Feedback

supportingInfo.explanation:
Changes Made

Two new stocks were added to the model: whatajigs (initial value 100) and balacks (initial value 200), each with their own inflows and outflows.

Whatajigs

  • whatajigs_inflow: Driven by 5% of base_stock_x (using constant whatajigs_growth_rate = 0.05)
  • whatajigs_outflow: Driven by 300% of balacks (using constant whatajigs_loss_rate = 3.0)

Balacks

  • balacks_inflow: Driven by 5% of whatajigs (using constant balacks_growth_rate = 0.05)
  • balacks_outflow: Driven by 3% of base_stock_x (using constant balacks_loss_rate = 0.03)

Feedback Loops Identified

A balancing loop exists between whatajigs and balacks: more balacks drain whatajigs faster, while more whatajigs feed balacks — this creates a predator-prey style dynamic. Additionally, base_stock_x acts as an external driver influencing both the growth of whatajigs and the depletion of balacks, connecting the new subsystem to the original model structure.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Additions

Three new stocks were added to the model based on the warehouse inventory descriptions:

Marticatenes starts at 50 units. Its inflow is 15% of existing_pool_alpha each month, creating a reinforcing link from the existing alpha pool into this new inventory. Its outflow is 20% of its own current level, forming a balancing (negative) feedback loop where the larger the stock, the faster it drains. This is a classic goal-seeking archetype tending toward equilibrium.

Refluppers starts at 75 units. Its inflow is 20% of marticatenes, creating a causal chain: existing_pool_alpha → marticatenes → refluppers. Its outflow is driven by 10% of existing_pool_beta, meaning the beta pool externally governs how fast refluppers deplete. This introduces a cross-chain dependency between the beta and the marticatenes/refluppers chain.

Exemintes starts at 120 units. Its inflow is a fixed constant of 8 units per month (represented as a named constant variable per modeling rules). Its outflow is 10% of its own current level, again forming a balancing feedback loop driving the stock toward a natural equilibrium of 80 units (8 / 0.10).

All fractional rates were extracted into named constant variables to avoid embedding raw numbers directly in flow equations. All pre-existing variable names were preserved exactly.
supportingInfo.title: Warehouse Inventory Causal Discovery Model

Please add the following to my model...
Throughout the process, there are initially thirty-five povals. Every day, this inventory gains from 30% of the current dominitoxings count. Simultaneously, each day the stock suffers depletion of 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate ninety auspongs. Every day, this inventory receives new additions of 20% of the current povals count. Simultaneously, each day the stock suffers depletion of a constant twelve auspongs.  Meanwhile, we have on hand forty-five dominitoxings. Every day, this inventory increases due to 8% of the current existing_reservoir_deltas count. Simultaneously, each day the stock loses 30% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Additions

Three new stocks were added to the existing model: povals, auspongs, and dominitoxings, each with their respective inflows and outflows.

Povals

Initialized at 35 units. Its inflow is driven by 30% of the current dominitoxings level (a cross-stock reinforcing link), and its outflow is a self-draining balancing loop at 20% of its own level. This creates a balancing loop on povals itself and a reinforcing inter-stock link from dominitoxings.

Auspongs

Initialized at 90 units. Its inflow is driven by 20% of the current povals level (another cross-stock reinforcing link), and its outflow is a constant drain of 12 units per day. This creates a goal-seeking (balancing) structure where auspongs will stabilize when the povals-driven inflow equals 12.

Dominitoxings

Initialized at 45 units. Its inflow is driven by 8% of the current existing_reservoir_delta level (linking the new subsystem back to the original model), and its outflow is a self-draining balancing loop at 30% of its own level.

Feedback Loop Closure

The chain existing_reservoir_delta → dominitoxings → povals → auspongs is now fully connected. Dominitoxings feeds povals, povals feeds auspongs, and dominitoxings is itself fed by existing_reservoir_delta from the original model. All fractional rates were extracted as named constant variables to avoid embedding magic numbers in equations.
supportingInfo.title: Povals Auspongs Dominitoxings Inventory Feedback Model

Please add the following to my model...
In our organization, we begin with one hundred ten pablanksills. Every quarter, this inventory gains from 6% growth relative to its current size. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of a constant eighteen pablanksills.  Meanwhile, we have on hand seventy posistorathers. Every quarter, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty-five new posistorathers. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock suffers depletion of 35% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate ninety-five crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory gets replenished by exactly eighteen new crypterals. Every quarter, this inventory is enhanced by 35% of the current posistorathers count. Simultaneously, each quarter the stock decreases by 22% of its current amount.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Model Additions

Pablanksills Stock

Added a new stock pablanksills initialized at 110. A reinforcing (positive) feedback loop is formed: the stock drives its own pablanksills_growth inflow at 6% per quarter (growth rate stored as a separate constant pablanksills_growth_rate). A constant outflow pablanksills_depletion of 18 per quarter (stored as pablanksills_depletion_constant) drains the stock. This creates a classic reinforcing growth with drain archetype.

Posistorathers Stock

Added a new stock posistorathers initialized at 70. A constant inflow posistorathers_inflow of 25 per quarter (stored as posistorathers_inflow_constant) replenishes the stock. A balancing (negative) feedback loop is formed: the stock drives its own posistorathers_depletion outflow at 35% per quarter (rate stored as posistorathers_depletion_rate). This is a classic goal-seeking or balancing loop archetype.

Crypterals Stock

Added a new stock crypterals initialized at 95. It receives two inflows: a constant crypterals_constant_inflow of 18 per quarter (stored as crypterals_constant_inflow_value), and a variable inflow crypterals_posistorathers_inflow equal to 35% of the current posistorathers stock (rate stored as crypterals_posistorathers_rate). This creates a cross-stock causal link from posistorathers to crypterals. A balancing loop is formed via the outflow crypterals_depletion at 22% of current crypterals (rate stored as crypterals_depletion_rate).

All original variables (existing_tank_epsilon, existing_tank_zeta, refill_epsilon, leak_epsilon, pump_zeta) are preserved unchanged.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I'm trying to do causal discovery, and extract every cause and effect relationship from the information I give you.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Four new stocks were added to the existing model: ocs (initial value 25), proptimatires (initial value 40), priaries (initial value 80), and houtals (initial value 60). Each stock has a dedicated inflow and outflow flow variable, and all numerical constants (rates and fixed values) are represented as separate auxiliary variables rather than embedded directly in equations.

  • ocs grows via ocs_inflow (15% of proptimatires) and shrinks via ocs_outflow (4% of existing_chamber_eta), creating a cross-stock dependency loop.
  • proptimatires grows via proptimatires_inflow (9% of existing_chamber_theta) and shrinks via proptimatires_outflow (25% of itself), forming a balancing loop on itself and feeding into both ocs and priaries.
  • priaries grows via priaries_inflow (10% of proptimatires) and shrinks via priaries_outflow (5% of houtals), linking proptimatires and houtals into a chain.
  • houtals grows via a constant inflow of 7 per week and shrinks via houtals_outflow (8% of itself), forming its own balancing loop while also driving priaries outflow.

All pre-existing variables (existing_chamber_eta, existing_chamber_theta, injection_eta, extraction_eta, feed_theta) were preserved without renaming.

Please add the following to my model...
In my business, the baseline inventory shows one hundred fifty outrances. Every hour, this inventory benefits from exactly twenty new outrances. Simultaneously, each hour the stock has outgoing 40% of its current amount. Simultaneously, each hour the stock is reduced through 10% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, our records indicate thirty illigents. Every hour, this inventory gains from 40% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock decreases by a constant five illigents.  Meanwhile, we have on hand sixty-five yelbs. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of 10% of the current outrances count. Simultaneously, each hour the stock loses 12% of whatever trazes are currently available.  Meanwhile, our records indicate eighty-five trazes. Every hour, this inventory receives new additions of exactly fifteen new trazes.
