variables.name: Vehicle Volume
variables.documentation: Index of the amount of traffic entering the road network relative to a normal reference level. It accumulates from underlying growth in driving and is reduced when drivers avoid or reschedule trips.

variables.name: Traffic Growth
variables.documentation: Growth in the number of trips taken, proportional to current volume (population and economic growth).

variables.name: Traffic Growth Rate
variables.documentation: Fractional weekly growth in driving demand.

variables.name: Trip Avoidance
variables.documentation: Drivers giving up, delaying or re-routing trips. Rises when congestion becomes intolerable, forming a balancing loop on traffic volume.

variables.name: Trip Avoidance Fraction
variables.documentation: Normal fraction of trips abandoned or shifted each week under reference congestion.

variables.name: Congestion Deterrence Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier showing how worsening congestion pushes people to avoid driving. Normal congestion (1) gives normal deterrence (1).

variables.name: Traffic Congestion
variables.documentation: Accumulated level of crowding and delay on the network relative to normal. It builds when demand exceeds effective capacity or crashes block lanes, and dissipates as queues clear.

variables.name: Congestion Formation
variables.documentation: Rate at which queues and delays build up, driven by demand relative to capacity and by lanes blocked by crashes.

variables.name: Congestion Formation Rate
variables.documentation: Scaling constant for how quickly congestion forms under normal demand pressure.

variables.name: Congestion Clearing
variables.documentation: Dissipation of queues once flow resumes; a first order decay of the congestion stock.

variables.name: Congestion Clearing Time
variables.documentation: Average time for congestion to dissipate once its cause is removed.

variables.name: Congestion Pressure
variables.documentation: Ratio of traffic demand to the capacity actually available. Values above one mean the road cannot absorb the flow.

variables.name: Effective Road Capacity
variables.documentation: Usable throughput of the network, equal to design capacity degraded by weather.

variables.name: Road Design Capacity
variables.documentation: Quality of road design: lane width, intersection clarity and throughput under ideal conditions. Poor design means a lower value.

variables.name: Weather Severity
variables.documentation: Exogenous index of adverse weather (rain, snow, fog) relative to typical conditions.

variables.name: Weather Capacity Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier by which bad weather reduces usable road capacity. Normal weather (1) leaves capacity unchanged (1).

variables.name: Weather Stress Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier capturing the extra mental load of driving in bad weather. Normal weather gives normal stress load.

variables.name: Accident Blockage Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier by which crashes on the network add to congestion formation through lane blockage and rubbernecking.

variables.name: Driver Stress
variables.documentation: Accumulated tension, anxiety and frustration carried by the driving population relative to normal. It is a stock because stress builds over repeated trips and only unwinds slowly.

variables.name: Stress Buildup
variables.documentation: Rate at which driving conditions add to accumulated stress: delays, being cut off or tailgated, and difficult weather.

variables.name: Stress Buildup Rate
variables.documentation: Normal weekly stress loading from driving under reference conditions.

variables.name: Stress Recovery
variables.documentation: Natural relaxation and recovery of drivers between trips, a first order decay of stress.

variables.name: Stress Recovery Time
variables.documentation: Average time for accumulated driving stress to dissipate through rest and recovery.

variables.name: Congestion Stress Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier translating stop and go conditions and delay into added driver stress. Normal congestion yields normal stress loading.

variables.name: Perceived Provocations
variables.documentation: Frequency with which drivers feel cut off, tailgated or honked at. It rises with how aggressive typical driving has become and with how many close interactions congestion forces.

variables.name: Provocation Stress Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier for how being provoked by other drivers raises accumulated stress.

variables.name: Provocation Trigger Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier for immediate retaliation: each perceived provocation is a spark that can directly start an incident.

variables.name: Impatience
variables.documentation: Degree to which drivers feel behind schedule and intolerant of delay, driven by how much time congestion costs them.

variables.name: Stress Aggression Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier showing how accumulated stress lowers the threshold for an angry outburst behind the wheel.

variables.name: Aggressive Driving Norm
variables.documentation: Socially learned expectation that aggressive driving is normal and acceptable. It accumulates as drivers repeatedly observe aggression and fades when aggression is discouraged.

variables.name: Norm Reinforcement
variables.documentation: Rate at which witnessing aggressive driving normalises it for other drivers.

variables.name: Norm Learning Rate
variables.documentation: Speed at which observed behaviour is absorbed into social driving norms.

variables.name: Observed Aggression Effect
variables.documentation: How visible aggressive behaviour is to other road users, scaling with the number of incidents happening.

variables.name: Norm Decay
variables.documentation: Unlearning of aggressive norms through forgetting, driver turnover and, faster, through enforcement and public education.

variables.name: Norm Decay Rate
variables.documentation: Baseline fractional rate at which aggressive driving norms erode.

variables.name: Norm Aggression Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier translating the prevailing social norm into individual willingness to behave aggressively.

variables.name: Aggressive Personality Share
variables.documentation: Share of the driving population with impulsive, hostile or competitive traits, relative to normal. Exogenous trait background of the population.

variables.name: Enforcement Deterrence Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier by which visible policing and awareness campaigns suppress the propensity to act aggressively.

variables.name: Aggression Propensity
variables.documentation: Overall readiness of the average driver to react aggressively, combining stress, learned norms, impatience, personality mix and deterrence.

variables.name: Road Rage Incidents
variables.documentation: Number of aggressive driving confrontations currently underway or recently occurring, relative to normal. Treated as a stock so that ongoing incidents remain visible to other drivers for a while.

variables.name: Incident Onset
variables.documentation: Rate at which new road rage episodes start: exposure (how many drivers are out there) times readiness to be aggressive times the spark of provocation.

variables.name: Baseline Incident Rate
variables.documentation: Normal rate of road rage episodes per unit of traffic under reference conditions.

variables.name: Incident Resolution
variables.documentation: Rate at which confrontations end or de-escalate.

variables.name: Incident Duration
variables.documentation: Average persistence of an incident and of its visibility to other drivers.

variables.name: Accidents
variables.documentation: Crashes currently on the network awaiting clearance, relative to normal. Accumulating them as a stock captures how crash scenes block lanes and feed congestion until cleared.

variables.name: Accident Occurrence
variables.documentation: Rate of new crashes, rising with exposure, with aggressive driving, and with fatigue and distraction.

variables.name: Baseline Accident Rate
variables.documentation: Normal crash rate per unit of traffic under reference behaviour.

variables.name: Rage Crash Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier by which tailgating, weaving and brake checking during rage episodes raise crash risk.

variables.name: Accident Clearance
variables.documentation: Rate at which crash scenes are cleared and the road is reopened.

variables.name: Accident Clearance Time
variables.documentation: Average time to clear a crash from the roadway.

variables.name: Driver Impairment
variables.documentation: Combined degradation of attention and judgement from lack of sleep and from phone use, texting or eating while driving.

variables.name: Driver Fatigue
variables.documentation: Exogenous index of sleep deprivation in the driving population relative to normal.

variables.name: Distracted Driving
variables.documentation: Exogenous index of in-car distraction such as phones, texting and eating, relative to normal.

variables.name: Impairment Crash Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier by which fatigue and distraction raise crash risk. Normal impairment gives normal risk.

variables.name: Enforcement and Awareness
variables.documentation: Accumulated policing presence, penalties and public education about aggressive driving. Built up in response to a visible safety problem and eroding as attention and budgets fade.

variables.name: Enforcement Investment
variables.documentation: Rate of adding enforcement and awareness capacity in response to the perceived severity of the road safety problem.

variables.name: Enforcement Response Rate
variables.documentation: How strongly authorities and campaigners respond to a given level of perceived problem.

variables.name: Enforcement Erosion
variables.documentation: Loss of enforcement presence and public attention over time as budgets and campaigns lapse.

variables.name: Enforcement Decay Rate
variables.documentation: Fractional weekly loss of enforcement and awareness capacity.

variables.name: Perceived Road Safety Problem
variables.documentation: Public and official sense of how bad things are on the roads, an average of visible rage episodes and crashes.

variables.name: Problem Pressure Effect
variables.documentation: Multiplier translating perceived severity into political and social pressure for enforcement and education.

errorExplanations.name: total_incubation
errorExplanations.problem: Should use DELAY3 with the 'Infection' flow as input, not the 'Exposed population' stock divided by a time constant.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Errors found and fixed

1. Total incubation — wrong residence time, wrong unit conversion, and a double-counted delay (this was the source of the unit warning).

Old formulation: DELAY3(Exposed_population/Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week, Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week)

Three separate problems:

  • Wrong parameter: the drain of the exposed stock was divided by the asymptomatic infectious period, a parameter that belongs to the asymptomatic recovery chain. The residence time in the exposed stock must be the average incubation time.
  • Wrong dimensional operation: dividing a per-day rate again by Days per week (Day/Week) gives Person·Week/Day², not Person/Week. To convert a delay expressed in days into the weekly time base you must divide the delay by Days per week, i.e. use Exposed_population/(Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week).
  • Double delay: the expression already drained the stock at a rate of stock-over-residence-time (a first-order delay), and then wrapped that drain in a third-order DELAY3 with the incubation time again. This applies the incubation delay twice and, because the delayed output is no longer tied to the current content of the stock, it can drive the exposed stock negative.

Fixed formulation: Exposed_population/(Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week) — a clean first-order drain that is dimensionally consistent (Person/Week) and can never empty the stock below zero. Because the asymptomatic period is no longer part of this calculation, its (erroneous) influence on total incubation was dropped; the asymptomatic period still correctly governs asymptomatic recovery.

2. Missing one-directional (uniflow) settings on every physical flow.

None of the flows were constrained to be non-negative. Infections, incubation, symptom onset, recoveries, deaths, imported cases and immunity loss are all strictly one-way processes; a negative value is physically meaningless and would silently move people backwards through the disease chain. All flows (Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity, Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad) are now marked one-directional.

3. Missing units and documentation on most variables. Every variable now carries units and an explanation, which is what allowed the dimensional error in point 1 to be located.

Formulations checked and confirmed correct (left unchanged)

  • Delay style consistency: Developing symptoms, Recovery without symptoms, Total exiting symptomatic infectious and Losing immunity all apply DELAY3 to the complete inflow of their stock. That is the correct way to build a third-order material (pipeline-like) delay: material is conserved, and the stock always equals the material still in transit, so it cannot go negative. Only Total incubation broke this rule by delaying a stock-derived drain, which is why it was the one changed.
  • Total population and Infectious population are simple sums and are correctly auxiliaries rather than stocks.
  • Cumulative COVID deaths is correctly a stock (a genuine accumulation) and is correctly excluded from Total population, since the deceased no longer make contacts.
  • Splitting fractions (Share of asymptomatic infections, Case fatality rate of COVID patients) correctly use a fraction and its complement so that the two branches sum to the total flow — no people are created or lost.
  • Infection uses the standard contact-based formulation (infectious × contacts × susceptible fraction × transmissibility) and is dimensionally consistent.
  • Time-driven graphical functions (Social distancing measures, Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad) are correctly driven by TIME; the (1,1) normalisation rule does not apply to time-based tables.
  • Time step: the shortest third-order delay is the presymptomatic period (about 0.43 weeks, i.e. 0.14 weeks per stage), so the existing small DT remains adequate.

No variables and no new causal links were added.

variables.name: Susceptible population
variables.documentation: People who can still catch COVID. Drained by new infections and replenished as recovered people lose immunity.

variables.name: Exposed population
variables.documentation: People who have been infected but are not yet infectious. They leave this stock after the incubation period, splitting into an asymptomatic and a presymptomatic branch.

variables.name: Recovered population
variables.documentation: People with temporary immunity after recovering from either a symptomatic or an asymptomatic infection.

variables.name: Infection
variables.documentation: Standard contact-based infection rate: infectious people times their contacts, times the chance a contact is susceptible, times the transmission probability per contact. Marked uniflow because infections can never be negative.

variables.name: Incubation
variables.documentation: The portion of people finishing incubation who will eventually develop symptoms; they move into the presymptomatic infectious stock.

variables.name: Recovery
variables.documentation: The surviving share of the people leaving the symptomatic stock.

variables.name: Initial Susceptible population
variables.documentation: Population at risk at the start of the simulation.

variables.name: Chance of contact with an susceptible person
variables.documentation: Fraction of the living population that is still susceptible, i.e. the probability that any given contact is with a susceptible person.

variables.name: Infection rate per contact
variables.documentation: Probability that a contact between an infectious and a susceptible person transmits the virus.

variables.name: Total population
variables.documentation: Algebraic sum of all living epidemiological states (deaths are excluded because they no longer take part in contacts). Correctly formulated as an auxiliary, not a stock, because it is a sum and not an accumulation.

variables.name: Average COVID incubation time
variables.documentation: Average time between being infected and becoming infectious, expressed in days.

variables.name: Presymptomatic infectious
inflows: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Infectious people who have not yet developed symptoms, including imported cases.

variables.name: Symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: People with symptomatic COVID who either recover or die.

variables.name: Asymptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Infectious people who never develop symptoms and always recover.

variables.name: Developing symptoms
variables.documentation: Third-order material delay of everything that enters the presymptomatic stock, delayed by the presymptomatic period converted from days to weeks. Because the delay is applied to the complete inflow it conserves material and the presymptomatic stock can never go negative.

variables.name: Recovery without symptoms
variables.documentation: Third-order material delay of the inflow to the asymptomatic stock, delayed by the average asymptomatic infectious period converted from days to weeks.

variables.name: Asymptomatic incubation
variables.documentation: The portion of people finishing incubation who will never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Share of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Fraction of infections that remain asymptomatic (literature range roughly 25% to 80%).

variables.name: Total incubation
variables.documentation: Total rate at which exposed people finish incubation. Formulated as the exposed stock divided by the average incubation time (converted from days to weeks). This replaces the previous formulation, which used the asymptomatic infectious period as the residence time, divided rather than multiplied by the day-to-week conversion, and additionally wrapped the stock drain in a DELAY3 (double counting the incubation delay).

variables.name: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-based importation of infectious travellers that seeds the epidemic. Time-based graphical functions are not normalised through (1,1).

variables.name: Average period of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Average number of days an asymptomatic person stays infectious.

variables.name: Dying of COVID
variables.documentation: The fatal share of the people leaving the symptomatic stock.

variables.name: Case fatality rate of COVID patients
variables.documentation: Fraction of symptomatic cases that end in death.

variables.name: Presymptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average number of days a person is infectious before symptoms appear.

variables.name: Losing immunity
variables.documentation: Third-order material delay of everything entering the recovered stock, delayed by the average immunity period. Because the delay is applied to the full inflow, material is conserved and the recovered stock cannot go negative.

variables.name: Average immunity period
variables.documentation: Average duration of post-infection immunity.

variables.name: Average length of symptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average duration of the symptomatic infectious phase.

variables.name: Infectious population
variables.documentation: Everyone able to transmit the virus. A simple sum, therefore an auxiliary rather than a stock.

variables.name: Contacts per person per week
variables.documentation: Effective contact frequency after the reduction achieved by social distancing.

variables.name: Social distancing measures
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-based policy stringency expressed as the fractional reduction of normal contacts.

variables.name: Cumulative COVID deaths
variables.documentation: Running total of COVID deaths. Correctly a stock because it accumulates a flow, and correctly excluded from the living total population.

variables.name: Normal number of contacts per week
variables.documentation: Contacts per person per week in the absence of any restrictions.

variables.name: Days per week
variables.documentation: Unit conversion constant used to translate delay times expressed in days into the model's weekly time base.

variables.name: Total exiting symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Rate at which people leave the symptomatic stock, obtained as a third-order material delay of the inflow. It is then split into recovery and death.

errorExplanations.name: developing_symptoms
errorExplanations.problem: Should use the flows 'Incubation + Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad' as input to DELAY3, not the stock 'Presymptomatic infectious' divided by a time constant.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Errors found and fixes

1. Developing symptoms — wrong parameter, wrong dimensions, and a non-conservative structure (the only substantive error).

Old equation: DELAY3(Presymptomatic_infectious/Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week, Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week)

Three distinct problems were stacked in this one formulation:

  • Wrong time constant. The outflow of the presymptomatic stock was being computed with the asymptomatic infectious period. The two clinical stages are unrelated; the presymptomatic stock must drain over the presymptomatic period.
  • Dimensional error (this is the unit warning that was reported). Dividing People by Days and then again by Days/Week gives People·Weeks/Days², not People/Week. The days-to-weeks conversion has to be applied to the duration (Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week), not as a second division of the rate.
  • Double delay / loss of conservation. The argument of the delay was already a drain of the stock, and then that drain was pushed through another third-order delay. A delayed drain is no longer tied to the current contents of the stock, so the presymptomatic stock could be emptied past zero (or hold people indefinitely) — particularly once the exogenous imported-case inflow starts and stops abruptly.

New equation: Presymptomatic_infectious/(Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week) — a first-order material drain of the stock over its average residence time, correctly converted to weeks.

Why first-order here and pipeline delays elsewhere: every other outflow in this model (Total incubation, Recovery without symptoms, Total exiting symptomatic infectious, Losing immunity) is a third-order pipeline delay of exactly the total inflow of the stock it drains, which is a conservative and legitimate cohort formulation. The presymptomatic stock is the one exception: it has two inflows (domestic incubation plus imported cases), so no single-input pipeline delay can conserve it. A first-order drain of the stock itself is the safe, standard formulation and guarantees the stock can never go negative. Because the presymptomatic period is short (3 days) relative to the epidemic's dynamics, the loss of cohort sharpness is negligible.

As a consequence, the spurious dependence of Developing symptoms on Average period of asymptomatic infections was removed; that parameter now correctly influences only the asymptomatic recovery flow.

2. Missing one-directional (uniflow) settings on every flow.

None of the flows were marked as one-directional. Infections, incubation completions, symptom onsets, recoveries, deaths, imported cases and immunity losses are all physically irreversible processes; with delayed formulations and sharply changing exogenous inputs, a delay can transiently return a small negative value and push people backwards through the disease stages. All nine flows are now constrained to be non-negative.

3. Missing integration method specification.

The run specification did not state a solver. It is now explicitly Euler, which is appropriate for this delay-based model; the existing very small time step (1/128 week) is retained because the shortest delay stage in the model (a third of the 3-day incubation period, ≈0.14 week) requires a step far below it.

Items checked and confirmed correct (no change made):

  • Total population and Infectious population are algebraic sums and are correctly auxiliaries rather than stocks; Total population correctly excludes cumulative deaths, since the dead make no contacts.
  • Total incubation and Total exiting symptomatic infectious are correctly auxiliaries that are then split into two real flows each.
  • Cumulative COVID deaths is correctly a stock with a single inflow.
  • The DELAY3 pipeline formulations for incubation, asymptomatic recovery, symptomatic exit and immunity loss each take as input the exact total inflow of the stock they drain, so they conserve people and are left in the original style.
  • The two time-driven table functions (imported cases, social distancing) legitimately use TIME as their input and are exogenous scenario data, so they are unchanged.

variables.name: Susceptible population
variables.documentation: People who can still catch COVID. Increased by people whose immunity wanes, drained by new infections.

variables.name: Exposed population
variables.documentation: People who have been infected but are not yet infectious (latent period). Its only inflow is Infection and its outflows sum exactly to Total incubation, so the third-order pipeline delay used here conserves people.

variables.name: Recovered population
variables.documentation: People with temporary immunity. Drained by loss of immunity, which is the pipeline-delayed version of exactly the two inflows, so the stock is conserved and cannot go negative.

variables.name: Infection
variables.documentation: Standard mass-action infection rate: infectious people times their contacts, times the probability a contact is susceptible, times the transmission probability per contact. Marked uniflow because infections can never be negative.

variables.name: Incubation
variables.documentation: The part of people finishing the latent period who will eventually show symptoms. Uniflow: people can only move forward through the disease stages.

variables.name: Recovery
variables.documentation: Symptomatic people who survive the illness. Uniflow: recoveries cannot be negative.

variables.name: Initial Susceptible population
variables.documentation: Initial size of the fully susceptible population at the start of the epidemic.

variables.name: Chance of contact with an susceptible person
variables.documentation: Probability that a random contact of an infectious person is susceptible, assuming random mixing in the living population.

variables.name: Infection rate per contact
variables.documentation: Probability that a contact between an infectious and a susceptible person transmits the virus.

variables.name: Total population
variables.documentation: Sum of all living epidemiological states (deaths are excluded because they no longer make contacts). This is an algebraic sum, therefore an auxiliary and not a stock.

variables.name: Average COVID incubation time
variables.documentation: Average latent period between infection and becoming infectious, expressed in days.

variables.name: Presymptomatic infectious
inflows: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Infectious people who do not yet show symptoms. Because this stock has two inflows (domestic incubation and imported cases), its outflow is formulated as a first-order material drain of the stock itself so that the stock is always conserved and can never go negative.

variables.name: Symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: People who are ill and infectious. Its single inflow is Developing symptoms and its outflows sum exactly to Total exiting symptomatic infectious, so the pipeline delay conserves people.

variables.name: Asymptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Infectious people who never develop symptoms. Single inflow and single (pipeline-delayed) outflow keep the stock conserved.

variables.name: Developing symptoms
variables.documentation: Rate at which presymptomatic infectious people become symptomatic. Formulated as a first-order drain: the presymptomatic stock divided by the presymptomatic period converted from days into weeks. This replaces an earlier equation that mistakenly used the asymptomatic period, divided twice, and applied a further pipeline delay, which was dimensionally wrong and did not conserve the stock when imported cases entered it.

variables.name: Recovery without symptoms
variables.documentation: Asymptomatic people recovering after the average asymptomatic infectious period. A third-order pipeline delay of the only inflow to the asymptomatic stock, so the stock stays conserved.

variables.name: Asymptomatic incubation
variables.documentation: The part of people finishing the latent period who will never show symptoms.

variables.name: Share of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Fraction of infections that never become symptomatic. Estimates range between 25% and 80%.

variables.name: Total incubation
variables.documentation: Total rate at which exposed people become infectious, computed as the pipeline-delayed infection rate. Because Infection is the only inflow to the exposed stock, this outflow formulation conserves people. It is an auxiliary because it is split into two actual flows.

variables.name: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-dependent import of infectious travellers seeding the epidemic. Uniflow because imports can only add people.

variables.name: Average period of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Average number of days an asymptomatic person remains infectious.

variables.name: Dying of COVID
variables.documentation: Fatal fraction of the people leaving the symptomatic state. Uniflow because deaths cannot be negative.

variables.name: Case fatality rate of COVID patients
variables.documentation: Fraction of symptomatic cases that end in death.

variables.name: Presymptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average number of days a person is infectious before symptoms appear.

variables.name: Losing immunity
variables.documentation: Recovered people returning to the susceptible pool after immunity wanes. The delay input is exactly the sum of the two inflows to the recovered stock, so the stock is conserved.

variables.name: Average immunity period
variables.documentation: Average duration of post-infection immunity in weeks.

variables.name: Average length of symptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average duration of symptomatic illness before recovery or death, in weeks.

variables.name: Infectious population
variables.documentation: All people currently able to transmit the virus. An algebraic sum, therefore an auxiliary.

variables.name: Contacts per person per week
variables.documentation: Effective contact frequency, reduced from the normal level by the strength of social distancing measures.

variables.name: Social distancing measures
variables.documentation: Exogenous policy scenario: fractional reduction of normal contacts over time.

variables.name: Cumulative COVID deaths
variables.documentation: Running total of deaths; a true accumulation with no outflow.

variables.name: Normal number of contacts per week
variables.documentation: Contacts per person per week in the absence of any distancing measures.

variables.name: Days per week
variables.documentation: Unit conversion constant used to translate clinical periods expressed in days into the weekly time base of the model.

variables.name: Total exiting symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Total rate of leaving the symptomatic state, computed as the pipeline-delayed inflow to that stock. It is an auxiliary because it is split into recoveries and deaths.

errorExplanations.name: recovery_without_symptoms
errorExplanations.problem: Should use DELAY3 with the 'Asymptomatic incubation' flow as input, not the 'Asymptomatic infectious' stock divided by a time constant.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Errors found and fixed

1. Recovery without symptoms — double delay and wrong units (this was the source of the reported unit warning)

  • Was: DELAY3(Asymptomatic_infectious/Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week, Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week)
  • Why wrong: Two independent problems. (a) Units: dividing a stock (People) by days and again by days-per-week yields People·Weeks/Days², not People/Week. The intent was to convert the period from days to weeks, which requires dividing by the period expressed in weeks, i.e. period/Days_per_week, not dividing twice. (b) Structure: the inner expression is already a complete first-order drain of the asymptomatic stock; wrapping it in a third-order pipeline delay delays the same cohort a second time, so asymptomatic people would stay infectious for roughly twice the intended duration and the stock would be drained on a rate that no longer reflects its own content.
  • Fixed to: Asymptomatic_infectious/(Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week) — a clean first-order drain with units People/Week. This also matches the causal structure already declared for this flow (it is driven by the asymptomatic stock, the average period, and the day/week conversion), unlike the other transitions which are declared as cohort pipelines driven by their upstream flows.

2. Missing one-way (uniflow) settings on every flow

  • Why wrong: Infections, incubation transitions, symptom onset, recoveries, deaths, imported cases and immunity loss are all strictly one-directional physical processes. Without the constraint, numerical transients in the third-order delays (or a negative distancing/graphical value) could push a rate negative and, for example, resurrect dead people or un-infect people.
  • Fixed: all flows (Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity, Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad) are now marked one-directional.

3. Chance of contact with an susceptible person — unprotected division

  • Why wrong: dividing by Total_population fails if the living population is ever zero.
  • Fixed: switched to the safe-division operator (//), leaving the meaning unchanged.

4. Missing documentation and rationale on all variables

  • Every variable now carries an explanation of what it represents and why it is computed that way, which is what makes delay-style choices auditable.

Checks performed that revealed no error (left unchanged)

  • Aggregations are auxiliaries, not stocks. Total population, Infectious population, Total incubation and Total exiting symptomatic infectious are algebraic sums/splits and are correctly typed as auxiliaries.
  • Delay choice is appropriate. All remaining DELAY3 uses (Total incubation, Developing symptoms, Total exiting symptomatic infectious, Losing immunity) are material-conserving transit delays of cohorts, not attempts at averaging, so a delay function — rather than a smoothing function — is the correct choice. Each one delays the inflow of its stock, which guarantees the corresponding stock cannot go negative. Note the deliberate distinction now in the model: stages whose exit is declared to depend on the upstream flow use pipeline delays, while the asymptomatic stage, whose exit is declared to depend on its own stock, uses a first-order drain.
  • Stock–flow consistency. No flow appears as both an inflow and an outflow of the same stock; Dying of COVID legitimately drains the symptomatic stock while filling cumulative deaths.
  • Branching fractions (Share of asymptomatic infections, Case fatality rate of COVID patients) correctly use the fraction and its complement so no people are created or lost at the splits.
  • Time-based graphical functions (Social distancing measures, Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad) are exogenous drivers of time and therefore correctly exempt from the (1,1) normalisation convention.
  • Time step of 1/128 week remains small relative to the shortest third-order delay stage (about 0.14 week), so the delays integrate accurately.

variables.name: Susceptible population
variables.documentation: People who can still catch COVID. Filled by people whose immunity wanes, drained by new infections.

variables.name: Exposed population
variables.documentation: People who have been infected but are not yet infectious. They leave along two branches: those who will remain asymptomatic and those who will become presymptomatic.

variables.name: Recovered population
variables.documentation: People with temporary immunity after recovering from a symptomatic or asymptomatic infection.

variables.name: Infection
variables.documentation: Standard force-of-infection formulation: infectious people times their contacts, times the chance a contact is susceptible, times the transmission probability per contact. Marked uniflow because infections can never run backwards.

variables.name: Incubation
variables.documentation: The part of the cohort finishing incubation that will eventually show symptoms; it enters the presymptomatic infectious stock.

variables.name: Recovery
variables.documentation: The surviving share of the cohort leaving the symptomatic stage.

variables.name: Initial Susceptible population
variables.documentation: Size of the population at the start of the epidemic, all assumed susceptible.

variables.name: Chance of contact with an susceptible person
variables.documentation: Probability that a random contact is susceptible, assuming random mixing. Safe division is used so the calculation cannot fail if the living population were ever zero.

variables.name: Infection rate per contact
variables.documentation: Probability that a contact between an infectious and a susceptible person transmits the virus.

variables.name: Total population
variables.documentation: Living population: the algebraic sum of all disease states. Correctly kept as an auxiliary (a sum), not a stock, because it has no flows of its own.

variables.name: Average COVID incubation time
variables.documentation: Average time from infection to becoming infectious.

variables.name: Presymptomatic infectious
inflows: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Infectious people who do not yet show symptoms, including imported cases.

variables.name: Symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: People who are infectious and showing symptoms; they either recover or die.

variables.name: Asymptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Infectious people who never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Developing symptoms
variables.documentation: Material-conserving pipeline (third-order) delay of everything that entered the presymptomatic stock, shifted by the presymptomatic period converted from days to weeks. This is a transit delay of a cohort, so DELAY3 is the correct function here.

variables.name: Recovery without symptoms
variables.documentation: CORRECTED. Asymptomatic people recover as a first-order drain of the asymptomatic stock: the stock divided by the average asymptomatic period expressed in weeks. The previous version divided the stock by the period and again by days per week (wrong units) and then wrapped that drain inside another third-order delay, delaying the same cohort twice.

variables.name: Asymptomatic incubation
variables.documentation: The part of the cohort finishing incubation that will never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Share of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Fraction of infections that stay asymptomatic (literature range roughly 25 to 80 percent).

variables.name: Total incubation
variables.documentation: All people finishing incubation, i.e. the infection cohort shifted by the incubation time converted to weeks. Kept as an auxiliary because it is only split into the two incubation flows.

variables.name: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-based import of infectious travellers. Time-based graphical functions do not need to pass through (1,1).

variables.name: Average period of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Average duration of infectiousness for people who never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Dying of COVID
variables.documentation: The fatal share of the cohort leaving the symptomatic stage. It leaves the living population and accumulates in cumulative deaths.

variables.name: Case fatality rate of COVID patients
variables.documentation: Fraction of symptomatic cases that end in death.

variables.name: Presymptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average time spent infectious before symptoms appear.

variables.name: Losing immunity
variables.documentation: Recovered cohorts return to the susceptible pool after the average immunity period. A pipeline delay of the recovery flows is used, consistent with the cohort-progression style of the rest of the model, and it conserves people so the recovered stock cannot go negative.

variables.name: Average immunity period
variables.documentation: Average duration of post-infection immunity.

variables.name: Average length of symptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average time a case stays symptomatic and infectious before recovering or dying.

variables.name: Infectious population
variables.documentation: All people who can transmit the virus. Correctly an auxiliary sum rather than a stock.

variables.name: Contacts per person per week
variables.documentation: Effective contact frequency after social distancing reduces the normal contact rate.

variables.name: Social distancing measures
variables.documentation: Exogenous policy stringency over time, expressed as the fractional reduction in contacts. Time-based graphical function.

variables.name: Cumulative COVID deaths
variables.documentation: Running total of deaths, an accumulation of the death flow.

variables.name: Normal number of contacts per week
variables.documentation: Contact frequency per person in the absence of any restrictions.

variables.name: Days per week
variables.documentation: Unit conversion used to express delays specified in days in the model's weekly time base.

variables.name: Total exiting symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Everyone leaving the symptomatic stage: the cohort that developed symptoms, shifted by the symptomatic duration. It is then split into recoveries and deaths.

errorExplanations.name: influx_of_presymptomatic_infectious_people_from_abroad
errorExplanations.problem: The graphical function should use TIME as an input, not DT (DT).

supportingInfo.explanation:
Formulation errors found and fixed

1. Stock outflows formulated as delayed inflows (5 occurrences) — the most serious error. In a stock-and-flow model an outflow must be computed from the stock it drains, never from a delayed copy of the inflow. Using DELAY3(inflow, time) creates a flow that is completely disconnected from the level it empties: the stock can be driven negative, material is not conserved, and — critically for an epidemic model — the balancing feedback from the state back onto its own drain is missing, so the aging chain does not behave like a real residence-time process. These were fixed by the standard first-order exponential-delay formulation, stock / average residence time, keeping the day-to-week unit conversion via Days per week that the original used:

  • Total incubation: was DELAY3(Infection, Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week) → now Exposed_population/(Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week).
  • Developing symptoms: was DELAY3(Incubation + Influx..., Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week) → now Presymptomatic_infectious/(Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week). (The old form also double-counted the import stream: imported travellers were added to the stock and separately pushed through the delay.)
  • Recovery without symptoms: was DELAY3(Asymptomatic_incubation, ...) → now Asymptomatic_infectious/(Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week).
  • Total exiting symptomatic infectious: was DELAY3(Developing_symptoms, Average_length_of_symptomatic_period) → now Symptomatic_infectious/Average_length_of_symptomatic_period.
  • Losing immunity: was DELAY3(Recovery + Recovery_without_symptoms, Average_immunity_period) → now Recovered_population/Average_immunity_period.

These fixes restore the material-conserving structure and re-establish the balancing loops inherent to every aging chain (a bigger state drains itself faster). The causal links that merely reflected the old delayed-inflow wiring (for example incubation and imports driving symptom onset) were replaced by the corresponding stock-to-drain links; no new external structure or policy loop was introduced.

2. Lookup driven by DT instead of TIME — variable: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad. The input to this time-based graphical function was the numerical time step, a tiny constant, so the import curve was frozen at essentially zero for the entire run and the epidemic could never be seeded. Fixed by driving the lookup with TIME, consistent with the way the Social distancing measures lookup is driven.

3. Missing one-directional constraints on flows. All physically one-way processes (Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity, and the import flow) are now marked as non-negative flows, so no process can run backwards under numerical transients.

4. Housekeeping checks that were already correct and were retained. Total population and Infectious population are simple algebraic sums and correctly remain auxiliaries rather than stocks; Cumulative COVID deaths is correctly an accumulation with an inflow only; the deaths stock is correctly excluded from the living population used in the contact-probability calculation; and the contagion equation retains its standard contacts × transmissibility × susceptible-fraction form. Units and documentation were added throughout, and the scientific-notation initial population was written out explicitly.

errorExplanations.name: social_distancing_measures
errorExplanations.problem: The graphical function should use TIME as an input, not DT (DT).

supportingInfo.explanation:
Errors found and fixed

1. Social distancing measures — wrong lookup input (DT) The policy scenario is a time based graphical function, but its equation was DT, the simulation time step. With DT = 0.0078125 the lookup would have been evaluated permanently at essentially x = 0, returning zero distancing forever, and the whole policy loop would have been silently dead. Fixed: the equation is now TIME, so the lookup traces the intended policy path over the 60 week horizon. (Being time based, it correctly does not need to pass through the point (1,1).)

2. Chance of contact with an susceptible person — unprotected division The susceptible fraction divided by Total_population with no protection. Fixed: rewritten with the safe-division operator (Susceptible_population // Total_population) so a zero population cannot crash the run.

3. All flows were missing the one-way (uniflow) specification Every flow here is a physically one-directional process (contagion, incubation, symptom onset, recovery, death, importation, immunity loss). Without the uniflow restriction, numerical transients in the third order delays could push a flow negative, resurrecting dead people or un-infecting people. Fixed: Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity and Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad are now all marked one-directional.

4. Missing causal polarities A large number of links (contagion inputs, delay times, population sums, split fractions, unit conversion) carried no polarity, so the loop structure could not be read. Fixed: polarity and reasoning are now supplied for every link. Note especially the sign pattern that defines the two governing loops: the balancing depletion loop (Infection → Susceptible → susceptible fraction → Infection) and the reinforcing contagion loop (Infection → Exposed → infectious stocks → Infection).

5. Hard-coded number cleaned up Initial Susceptible population was written in exponent shorthand (1.7e+07); it is now written plainly as 17000000. All other numeric values were already properly abstracted into named parameters, and the day-to-week conversions correctly use the named Days per week rather than a bare 7 inside the delay expressions.

Checked and deliberately left unchanged

  • Third order material delays. Every stage outflow is formulated as DELAY3 of that stage's inflow (Total incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery without symptoms, Total exiting symptomatic infectious, Losing immunity). This is a pipeline (material) delay, not an averaging device, and with constant delay times it conserves people exactly: each stock drains precisely what entered it. This is the consistent style of the model, so it was preserved rather than converted to first order drains.
  • Total population and Infectious population are auxiliaries, not stocks. They are simple algebraic sums, so auxiliary is the correct type; making them stocks would be a classic formulation error.
  • Total population correctly excludes Cumulative COVID deaths — the dead must not appear in the mixing pool that determines the susceptible fraction.
  • Total incubation and Total exiting symptomatic infectious are rate-valued auxiliaries that are split into two flows each; the split uses complementary fractions (share asymptomatic / case fatality rate and their complements), so no people are created or lost at the splits.
  • Time step. DT of 1/128 week is kept: the shortest pipeline is 3/7 of a week split into three stages, so a very small step is required for accurate Euler integration.

variables.name: Susceptible population
variables.documentation: People who can still catch COVID. It is drained by new infections and refilled by people whose immunity has waned. Initialized at the size of the modeled population.

variables.name: Exposed population
variables.documentation: Infected but not yet infectious people. The outflows split the delayed infection stream into the symptomatic-track and asymptomatic-track pipelines.

variables.name: Recovered population
variables.documentation: People with temporary immunity after recovering from a symptomatic or asymptomatic infection. Drained as immunity wanes.

variables.name: Infection
variables.documentation: Standard mass-action contagion: infectious people times contacts per week times the chance a contact is susceptible times transmission probability per contact. Marked uniflow because infections cannot run backwards.

variables.name: Incubation
variables.documentation: The part of people leaving the exposed stage that will eventually develop symptoms. Uses the complement of the asymptomatic share so the two exit flows exactly add up to the total leaving incubation.

variables.name: Recovery
variables.documentation: Survivors leaving the symptomatic stage. Together with deaths it exactly equals everybody exiting the symptomatic pipeline, so no people are created or lost.

variables.name: Initial Susceptible population
variables.documentation: Size of the population at the start of the epidemic; used only to initialize the susceptible stock.

variables.name: Chance of contact with an susceptible person
variables.documentation: Fraction of the living population that is still susceptible, i.e. the probability that a random contact is with a susceptible person. Safe division is used so the model cannot fail if the population ever reaches zero.

variables.name: Infection rate per contact
variables.documentation: Probability that a contact between an infectious and a susceptible person transmits the virus.

variables.name: Total population
variables.documentation: Sum of all living epidemiological states. Correctly an auxiliary (an algebraic sum), not a stock, and correctly excludes cumulative deaths because dead people are no longer part of the mixing population.

variables.name: Average COVID incubation time
variables.documentation: Average number of days between being infected and becoming infectious.

variables.name: Presymptomatic infectious
inflows: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Infectious people who do not yet show symptoms, fed by domestic incubation and by imported cases.

variables.name: Symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: People with symptomatic COVID who either recover or die.

variables.name: Asymptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Infectious people who never develop symptoms and always recover.

variables.name: Developing symptoms
variables.documentation: Third order material delay of everything that entered the presymptomatic stock, so that the presymptomatic stage empties exactly what it received after the presymptomatic period. The delay time is converted from days to weeks with days per week.

variables.name: Recovery without symptoms
variables.documentation: Third order material delay of the asymptomatic inflow, so the asymptomatic stock is emptied exactly after the average asymptomatic infectious period, expressed in weeks.

variables.name: Asymptomatic incubation
variables.documentation: The share of people leaving the exposed stage who will never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Share of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Fraction of infections that remain asymptomatic (literature range roughly 25 to 80 percent).

variables.name: Total incubation
variables.documentation: Total rate at which people finish incubating, formulated as a third order material delay of new infections so that the exposed stock drains exactly what it received. It is an auxiliary rate that is split into the symptomatic and asymptomatic exit flows.

variables.name: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time dependent seeding of imported infectious travellers. It is a time based graphical function, so it uses TIME as input and does not need to pass through the point (1,1).

variables.name: Average period of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Average number of days an asymptomatic person stays infectious.

variables.name: Dying of COVID
variables.documentation: The fatal fraction of people leaving the symptomatic stage. Uniflow because deaths cannot be undone.

variables.name: Case fatality rate of COVID patients
variables.documentation: Fraction of symptomatic cases that end in death.

variables.name: Presymptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average number of days a person is infectious before symptoms appear.

variables.name: Losing immunity
variables.documentation: Third order material delay of everything that entered the recovered stock, returning people to susceptibility after the average immunity period. The delay time is already in weeks, so no day conversion is needed.

variables.name: Average immunity period
variables.documentation: Average duration of post infection immunity in weeks.

variables.name: Average length of symptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average duration of the symptomatic infectious stage in weeks.

variables.name: Infectious population
variables.documentation: All people currently able to transmit the virus. An algebraic sum, therefore an auxiliary rather than a stock.

variables.name: Contacts per person per week
variables.documentation: Effective contact frequency: the normal contact rate reduced by the fractional strength of social distancing measures.

variables.name: Social distancing measures
variables.documentation: Exogenous policy scenario giving the fractional reduction of contacts over time. It is a time based lookup and therefore must be driven by TIME.

variables.name: Cumulative COVID deaths
variables.documentation: Running total of COVID deaths; an accumulation with no outflow.

variables.name: Normal number of contacts per week
variables.documentation: Contacts a person has per week in the absence of any distancing measures.

variables.name: Days per week
variables.documentation: Unit conversion constant used to translate delay times expressed in days into the week time base of the model.

variables.name: Total exiting symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Rate at which people finish the symptomatic stage, formulated as a third order material delay of the inflow so the symptomatic stock is conserved. It is split into recovery and death.

errorExplanations.name: total_population
errorExplanations.problem: Total population should be an auxiliary/converter variable that sums the population stocks, not a stock.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Errors found and fixes

1. Total population was formulated as a stock fed by a "net flow" that was actually a sum of levels (aggregation error).

  • What was wrong: Total population net flow was typed as a flow but its equation was Susceptible + Exposed + Asymptomatic + Presymptomatic + Symptomatic + Recovered — a quantity of people, not a rate of people per week. Integrating a level as if it were a rate makes Total population grow without bound (roughly the population times elapsed time), which corrupts Chance of contact with an susceptible person and therefore the whole infection loop. This is exactly what the unit warning flagged (Person vs. Person/Week).
  • Additional consequence: the stock's initial value was 0, so at time zero the contact-probability calculation divided by zero.
  • How it was fixed: Total population net flow is now an auxiliary measured in People holding the same six-stock sum (its equation is unchanged, only its type and units are corrected), and Total population is now an auxiliary that takes that value directly instead of accumulating it. Simple sums must be algebraic auxiliaries, never stocks. Since names could not be changed, the legacy "net flow" name is retained as a pass-through aggregation; ideally the two would be merged into a single auxiliary called Total population.

2. Susceptible population initialization / division-by-zero risk.

  • What was wrong: with total population starting at zero, the susceptible share was undefined at t = 0.
  • How it was fixed: because total population is now the algebraic sum of the stocks, it equals Initial Susceptible population at t = 0 and is strictly positive throughout, so the ratio is always well defined.

3. Missing one-directional (uniflow) settings on every physical flow.

  • What was wrong: infections, incubation, symptom onset, recoveries, deaths, imported arrivals and immunity loss are irreversible processes, but none were constrained. Numerical undershoot in the third-order delays or a negative table value could otherwise push people backwards through the disease stages.
  • How it was fixed: Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity and Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad are all marked as one-directional. Total population net flow is no longer a flow at all.

4. Relationship polarities were missing on most links.

  • What was wrong: over half the causal links carried no polarity, so the reinforcing contagion loop and the balancing susceptible-depletion loop were not readable from the structure.
  • How it was fixed: every link now carries an explicit polarity and reasoning. Note in particular the delay-time constants (incubation time, presymptomatic period, asymptomatic period, symptomatic period, immunity period) which are negative on their flows because a longer pipeline lowers the current outflow rate, and Days per week which is positive because it shortens day-based delays when expressed in weeks.

Formulations checked and deliberately left unchanged

  • The third-order pipeline delays (Total incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery without symptoms, Total exiting symptomatic infectious, Losing immunity) are correct uses of a material delay: they delay the cohort that entered each stage rather than averaging a signal, and they conserve people. They are internally consistent in style, so no substitution with SMOOTH (which is for averaging, not for aging a cohort) was made.
  • Splits using the structural complement (1 - Share of asymptomatic infections, 1 - Case fatality rate, 1 - Social distancing measures) are correct and guarantee that the branches sum to the total leaving each stage.
  • Both time-driven table functions (imported cases, social distancing) legitimately use TIME as their input and are exempt from the (1,1) normalization convention.
  • Infectious population and Cumulative COVID deaths were already correctly typed as an auxiliary sum and a true accumulation respectively.

variables.documentation: People who can still catch COVID. It is drained by new infections and refilled by people whose immunity wanes. Initialized with the starting susceptible population so that the total population is non-zero at time zero.

variables.name: Exposed population
variables.documentation: People who have been infected but are not yet infectious (latent period). Emptied by the two incubation flows, which split the cohort into future symptomatic and asymptomatic cases.

variables.name: Recovered population
variables.documentation: People with temporary immunity after recovering from either a symptomatic or an asymptomatic infection. Drained as immunity wanes.

variables.name: Infection
variables.documentation: Standard mass-action infection rate: infectious people times their contacts per week times the probability that a contact is susceptible times the transmission probability per contact. Marked one-directional because infections can never run backwards.

variables.name: Incubation
variables.documentation: The share of people finishing incubation who will go on to develop symptoms. Uses the structural complement (1 - asymptomatic share) so the two incubation flows always sum exactly to the total leaving the exposed stock.

variables.name: Recovery
variables.documentation: The survivors among those finishing the symptomatic period. Together with deaths it exactly accounts for everyone leaving the symptomatic stock.

variables.name: Initial Susceptible population
variables.documentation: Size of the population at risk at the start of the simulation.

variables.name: Chance of contact with an susceptible person
variables.documentation: Probability that a random contact is with someone still susceptible. This is the depletion (balancing) term of the epidemic loop. It is now safe because total population is an algebraic sum of the stocks and is therefore strictly positive from time zero.

variables.name: Infection rate per contact
variables.documentation: Probability that a contact between an infectious and a susceptible person results in transmission.

variables.name: Total population
variables.documentation: Living population used to normalize the contact probability. It is an algebraic aggregation, not an accumulation, so it is computed each step from the population aggregate rather than integrated. It takes its value from the aggregation variable that sums all six population stocks.

variables.name: Average COVID incubation time
variables.documentation: Average latent period between infection and becoming infectious.

variables.name: Presymptomatic infectious
inflows: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Infectious people who do not yet show symptoms, including imported cases arriving from abroad.

variables.name: Symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: People currently ill with symptoms. They leave either by recovering or by dying.

variables.name: Asymptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Infectious people who never develop symptoms; they all recover.

variables.name: Developing symptoms
variables.documentation: Material delay of everything entering the presymptomatic stock (domestic incubation plus imported cases) by the presymptomatic period, converted from days to weeks. Consistent with the pipeline-delay style used throughout the model and mass conserving.

variables.name: Recovery without symptoms
variables.documentation: Material delay of the asymptomatic inflow by the average asymptomatic infectious period, converted from days to weeks.

variables.name: Asymptomatic incubation
variables.documentation: The share of people finishing incubation who will never develop symptoms.

variables.name: Share of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: Fraction of infections that remain asymptomatic (empirical estimates range roughly between 25 and 80 percent).

variables.name: Total incubation
variables.documentation: Everyone finishing the latent period: the infection rate delayed by the incubation time, converted from days to weeks. It is then split into symptomatic and asymptomatic branches.

variables.name: Influx of presymptomatic infectious people from abroad
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-based arrival of infectious travellers that seeds and re-seeds the epidemic. Because it is a time-driven graphical function it does not need to pass through the point (1,1).

variables.name: Average period of asymptomatic infections
variables.documentation: How long asymptomatic people stay infectious.

variables.name: Dying of COVID
variables.documentation: The fatal share of those finishing the symptomatic period.

variables.name: Case fatality rate of COVID patients
variables.documentation: Fraction of symptomatic cases that end in death.

variables.name: Presymptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average time people are infectious before symptoms appear.

variables.name: Losing immunity
variables.documentation: Material delay of the two recovery flows by the average immunity period, returning people to the susceptible pool. This closes the reinfection loop and conserves people.

variables.name: Average immunity period
variables.documentation: Average duration of post-infection immunity.

variables.name: Average length of symptomatic period
variables.documentation: Average duration of symptomatic illness before recovery or death.

variables.name: Infectious population
variables.documentation: All people currently able to transmit the virus. A simple sum, therefore an auxiliary rather than a stock.

variables.name: Contacts per person per week
variables.documentation: Effective contact rate after policy restrictions reduce the normal contact rate. Uses the structural complement of the distancing intensity.

variables.name: Social distancing measures
variables.documentation: Exogenous, time-based intensity of restrictions (0 = no measures, 1 = complete cessation of contacts). Time-driven graphical function, so the (1,1) normalization does not apply.

variables.name: Cumulative COVID deaths
variables.documentation: Running total of deaths; a true accumulation with a single inflow and no outflow.

variables.name: Normal number of contacts per week
variables.documentation: Contacts per person per week in the absence of any restrictions.

variables.name: Days per week
variables.documentation: Unit conversion constant used to express delays specified in days in the model's weekly time base.

variables.name: Total exiting symptomatic infectious
variables.documentation: Everyone finishing the symptomatic period: the inflow to the symptomatic stock delayed by the illness duration. It is then split into recoveries and deaths.

variables.name: Total population net flow
variables.documentation: Algebraic aggregation of all six living population stocks. Despite its legacy name it is not a rate: it is a level-valued sum, so it is now an auxiliary measured in people rather than a flow measured in people per week.

errorExplanations.name: infectious_population
errorExplanations.problem: Infectious population should be an auxiliary/converter variable that sums the three infectious stocks, not a stock.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Formulation errors found and corrected

1. "Infectious population" was a stock accumulating a headcount (aggregation error)

  • What was wrong: It accumulated "Infectious population net flow", which was itself the sum of the three infectious stocks. A simple sum is an algebraic quantity, not an accumulation. As written, the model integrated a headcount over time, so the infectious population grew without bound (people were counted again every time step) and drove the infection rate to nonsense levels — the single most damaging error in the model.
  • Fix: "Infectious population net flow" is now an auxiliary equal to Symptomatic + Presymptomatic + Asymptomatic infectious (units: people), and "Infectious population" is now an auxiliary that takes that total directly. No accumulation occurs, and the reported unit warning ("people/week" declared, "people" implied) disappears.

2. Outflows written as third-order delays of the inflow instead of drains of the stock Every compartment outflow was formulated as a DELAY3 of the flow entering the compartment. This is the classic "disconnected stock" error: the outflow does not depend on the stock it empties, so people are not conserved, stocks can be driven negative, and the visible stock behaviour does not match the delay actually shaping the outflow (a single stock is by definition a first-order delay, not a third-order one). Each was converted to the standard first-order compartment drain — stock divided by average residence time — which keeps the pipeline logic implied by the model's parameters while guaranteeing conservation and non-negativity:

  • Total incubation: was DELAY3(Infection, incubation time); now Exposed_population/(Average_COVID_incubation_time/Days_per_week).
  • Developing symptoms: was DELAY3(Incubation + Influx from abroad, presymptomatic period); now Presymptomatic_infectious/(Presymptomatic_period/Days_per_week). This also fixes the fact that imported cases were being counted both as an inflow to the stock and inside its outflow expression.
  • Recovery without symptoms: was DELAY3(Asymptomatic incubation, ...); now Asymptomatic_infectious/(Average_period_of_asymptomatic_infections/Days_per_week).
  • Total exiting symptomatic infectious: was DELAY3(Developing symptoms, ...); now Symptomatic_infectious/Average_length_of_symptomatic_period.
  • Losing immunity: was DELAY3(Recovery + Recovery without symptoms, immunity period); now Recovered_population/Average_immunity_period, so immunity loss is proportional to the number of immune people actually present.

3. Missing one-directional flow settings None of the flows were constrained. Infection, Incubation, Asymptomatic incubation, Developing symptoms, Recovery, Recovery without symptoms, Dying of COVID, Losing immunity and the imported-case influx are all physically one-way processes; they are now marked as such so no compartment can be filled by a negative flow.

4. Checked and left unchanged (correct as given)

  • "Total population" is properly an auxiliary sum, and it correctly excludes cumulative deaths.
  • "Cumulative COVID deaths" is properly a stock, since it accumulates a genuine flow.
  • The two time-based lookups (imported cases, social distancing) legitimately use TIME as input and therefore do not need the usual normalisation through the point (1,1).

With these repairs the reinforcing contagion loop (more infectious people → more infections → more infectious people) and the two balancing loops (susceptible depletion, and the policy loop through contacts) all operate on conserved populations, so the epidemic peaks and subsides for the right structural reasons rather than through arithmetic artefacts.
supportingInfo.title: Fixed accumulating sum and disconnected delay outflows

testParams.name: Exponential Growth Pattern
testParams.prompt: Please create a model that demonstrates exponential growth behavior. The model must include a variable named 'output' that shows this behavior over time.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I need a model that exhibits exponential growth behavior in the 'output' variable.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Exponential growth occurs when the rate of increase is proportional to the current value. This creates a reinforcing feedback loop where larger values grow faster. Examples include compound interest, viral spread, and unconstrained population growth. A classic example would be compound interest or unconstrained population growth where the rate of growth is proportional to the current value.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Structure

The model is the canonical exponential growth (reinforcing loop) archetype, built with the minimum structure required:

  • output — a stock, because it is an accumulation that can change only through its flow.
  • growth — the single inflow to output, defined as output * fractional_growth_rate. This proportionality is what creates the reinforcing loop: more output → more growth → even more output.
  • fractional_growth_rate — the per-year fractional increase, abstracted out as its own named constant rather than being buried in the flow equation.
  • initial_output — the seed value of the stock, also abstracted into a named variable. It must be non-zero or the reinforcing loop has nothing to amplify.

Feedback loop

output → growth → output is a positive (reinforcing) loop with two positive links, producing smooth accelerating growth with a constant doubling time of about seven years at the chosen rate.

Modeling choices

  • The stock equation contains only its initial value (no INTEG), with the flow attached as an inflow.
  • growth is marked one-directional since a positive rate on a positive stock can never legitimately be negative.
  • No conditional logic, no graphical functions, and no hard-coded numbers inside expressions.
  • Simulation runs 50 years with a time step of 0.25 using Euler integration, which is ample to display several doublings.
supportingInfo.title: Reinforcing loop drives exponential output growth

relationships.reasoning: The amount added each period is proportional to the current level of output, so a larger stock generates a larger absolute addition.
relationships.polarityReasoning: An increase in output increases growth; a decrease in output decreases growth - they move in the same direction.

relationships.reasoning: Growth is the inflow that accumulates into the output stock.
relationships.polarityReasoning: A higher inflow raises the level of the stock, so both move in the same direction.

relationships.reasoning: The fractional rate scales how much of the current stock is added per unit of time.
relationships.polarityReasoning: A larger fractional growth rate produces a larger growth flow for the same level of output.

relationships.reasoning: The initial condition sets the starting point of the accumulation, and in exponential growth the whole trajectory scales with it.
relationships.polarityReasoning: A larger starting value yields a larger output at every later time.

variables.name: output
variables.documentation: The accumulating quantity of interest. It is a stock because it accumulates the additions made by its growth flow over time. Because its growth is proportional to its own size, it exhibits exponential growth.

variables.name: growth
variables.documentation: The rate at which output increases. It is proportional to the current level of output, which is the defining characteristic of exponential growth: the bigger the stock, the faster it grows. This closes the reinforcing feedback loop.

variables.name: fractional_growth_rate
variables.documentation: The constant fraction by which output grows each year. A positive value produces exponential growth; the larger the value, the shorter the doubling time.

variables.name: initial_output
variables.documentation: The starting level of output. It must be greater than zero, otherwise the reinforcing loop has nothing to amplify and the system stays at zero forever.

testParams.name: Exponential Decay Pattern
testParams.prompt: Please create a model that demonstrates exponential decay behavior. The model must include a variable named 'output' that shows this behavior over time.

additionalParameters.problemStatement: I need a model that exhibits exponential decay behavior in the 'output' variable.
additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge: Exponential decay occurs when the rate of decrease is proportional to the current value. This creates a negative feedback loop where the value decreases rapidly at first, then more slowly as it approaches zero. Examples include radioactive decay, drug elimination from the body, and temperature cooling. The output should show rapid decrease that slows over time, asymptotically approaching zero.

supportingInfo.explanation:
Structure created

  • output is a stock, since exponential decay is an accumulation being drained over time. Its initial value is set by initial output (no hard-coded number inside the stock equation).
  • decay is the single outflow from the stock, defined as output * decay_fraction. Making the loss proportional to the current level is exactly what produces exponential decay: fast loss at first, progressively slower as the stock shrinks, asymptotically approaching zero but never crossing it. The flow is marked one-directional so it can never run backwards and refill the stock.
  • decay fraction is the reciprocal of decay time constant, so the arbitrary speed parameter is named and isolated rather than buried in the flow equation. The time constant is the average lifetime of a unit (about 37% remaining after one time constant, half remaining after roughly 0.69 time constants).

Feedback logic

The model contains one balancing (negative) feedback loop: output → decay → output. More remaining quantity drives faster removal, which reduces the remaining quantity, which slows removal. A balancing loop acting on its own stock with no inflow is the canonical "draining" archetype and yields the smooth asymptotic approach to zero described in the background material (radioactive decay, drug elimination, Newtonian cooling toward ambient).

Run settings

The run spans 30 time units with a time step of 0.25 — roughly six decay time constants, enough to display the full curve from rapid initial drop to a near-zero tail, with a step small enough that the Euler solution closely tracks the true exponential.
