System Dynamics Model Overview

A quantitative Stock-Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed to represent the interaction between population dynamics and nonrenewable resource depletion across two dedicated modules: population and resource.

Module Architecture and Structural Formulations

1. Module population

  • Stock: population.count

    • Initial Value: 1,000 people
    • Inflows: population.births
    • Outflows: population.deaths, population.migrations
    • Description: Tracks the total number of individuals in the population over time.

  • Flow: population.births

    • Equation: count * birth_rate
    • Units: people/year
    • Description: Annual births generated proportionally from the population stock.

  • Flow: population.deaths

    • Equation: count * death_rate
    • Units: people/year
    • Description: Baseline mortality subtracting from the population stock.

  • Flow: population.migrations

    • Equation: MAX(0, count * (density_threshold - resource_density))
    • Units: people/year
    • Description: Outflow triggered when resource density drops below the critical threshold, directly proportional to total population and the resource density deficit without intermediate variables.

  • Parameter: population.birth rate

    • Equation: 0.05 (5% per year)
    • Units: 1/year

  • Parameter: population.death rate

    • Equation: 0.02 (2% per year)
    • Units: 1/year

  • Parameter: population.density threshold

    • Equation: 10
    • Units: resource units/person
    • Description: The critical per-capita resource availability threshold triggering emigration.

  • Ghost Variable: population.resource density

    • Source: resource.density
    • Units: resource units/person
    • Description: Cross-level ghost importing per-capita resource density from the resource module.

2. Module resource

  • Stock: resource.count

    • Initial Value: 50,000 resource units
    • Inflows: None (nonrenewable resource)
    • Outflows: resource.usage
    • Description: Aggregates remaining nonrenewable resource inventory.

  • Flow: resource.usage

    • Equation: usage_rate * population_count
    • Units: resource units/year
    • Description: Total resource extraction driven by population demand.

  • Parameter: resource.usage rate

    • Equation: 1
    • Units: resource units/(person*year)
    • Description: Per-capita resource consumption rate.

  • Auxiliary: resource.density

    • Equation: count // population_count
    • Units: resource units/person
    • Description: Ratio of remaining resource quantity to total population.

  • Ghost Variable: resource.population count

    • Source: population.count
    • Units: people
    • Description: Cross-level ghost importing current population into the resource module.

Feedback Loop Structure

The model's feedback loop analysis identifies five closed causal loops governing the system dynamics:

  1. Loop 1 (L1, Reinforcing / +): Population Reproduction

    • population.births (+) -> population.count (+) -> population.births
    • Generates exponential growth in the population stock during initial stages when resources are abundant.

  2. Loop 2 (L2, Balancing / -): Baseline Mortality

    • population.count (+) -> population.deaths (-) -> population.count
    • First-order natural mortality that counteracts unconstrained population accumulation.

  3. Loop 3 (L3, Balancing / -): Direct Population Migration Control

    • population.count (+) -> population.migrations (-) -> population.count
    • When resource density is below the threshold, larger population size increases migration volume, providing direct negative feedback on population count.

  4. Loop 4 (L4, Balancing / -): Resource Depletion and Migration Feedback

    • population.count (+) -> resource.population count (+) -> resource.usage (-) -> resource.count (+) -> resource.density (+) -> population.resource density (-) -> population.migrations (-) -> population.count
    • Coupling through cumulative resource extraction: higher population increases annual usage, permanently reducing the nonrenewable resource stock, driving down resource density, increasing migration pressure, and thereby decreasing population.

  5. Loop 5 (L5, Balancing / -): Per-Capita Dilution and Migration Feedback

    • population.count (+) -> resource.population count (-) -> resource.density (+) -> population.resource density (-) -> population.migrations (-) -> population.count
    • Immediate per-capita dilution: a higher population instantly reduces available density for any given resource stock level, triggering migration to relieve population pressure.

additionalParameters.backgroundKnowledge:
Please rely on the following expert knowledge as much as possible when creating your model.


            At a certain business, employees are sorted in a three-role hierarchy.
            New hirees start with the "rookie" status.
            Rookies that perform well are promoted to associates.
            Associates that perform well are promoted to partners.
            To keep the hierarchy stable, the business promotes a strict percentage of each role every year.
            Some employees may also leave the company, whether due to personal reasons or exceptionally poor performance.
            A stable percentage of employees at each level of the company leave the company each year.
            The business also onboards a constant number of new hirees every year.

            Create a model with three modules named 'rookies', 'associates', and 'partners'.
            
            Use the following component names within each module as appropriate:        
            count, 
            promotions, departures, hires,
            promotion_rate, departure_rate, hire_rate
            
            When creating a ghost component, preserve the name of the original component, including the module prefix (separated by a space rather than a period).
            So, a ghost of "module1.component" in module2 should be named "module2.module1 component".

Dynamic Structure and Formulation

The corporate hierarchy system is formulated as a three-stage aging chain partitioned across three distinct modules: rookies, associates, and partners.

rookies                          associates                          partners
+--------------+                 +--------------+                    +--------------+
| rookies.count|--promotions---> |associates.   |--promotions------> |partners.count|
|              |                 |count         |                    |              |
+-------+------+                 +-------+------+                    +-------+------+
        |                                |                                   |
    departures                       departures                          departures

Module Architecture and Equations

  1. Module rookies:

    • Stock rookies.count: Initial value = 100 people.
      • Inflows: rookies.hires
      • Outflows: rookies.promotions, rookies.departures
      • Units: people
    • Flow rookies.hires: Direct onboarding flow.
      • Equation: hire_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Flow rookies.promotions: Promotions to the associate tier.
      • Equation: count * promotion_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Flow rookies.departures: Turnover and performance exits.
      • Equation: count * departure_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Parameter rookies.hire_rate: Constant annual onboarding intake.
      • Equation: 20
      • Units: people/year
    • Parameter rookies.promotion_rate: Fixed annual promotion fraction.
      • Equation: 0.15
      • Units: 1/year
    • Parameter rookies.departure_rate: Fixed annual departure fraction.
      • Equation: 0.05
      • Units: 1/year

  2. Module associates:

    • Ghost Variable associates.rookies promotions: Cross-module reference representing incoming promotions from the rookie tier.
      • Source: rookies.promotions
      • Units: people/year
    • Flow associates.hires: Onboarding flow into the associate pool sourced from rookie promotions.
      • Equation: rookies_promotions
      • Units: people/year
    • Stock associates.count: Mid-tier workforce stock. Initial value = 50 people.
      • Inflows: associates.hires
      • Outflows: associates.promotions, associates.departures
      • Units: people
    • Flow associates.promotions: Promotions to partner status.
      • Equation: count * promotion_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Flow associates.departures: Turnover exits.
      • Equation: count * departure_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Parameter associates.promotion_rate: Fixed promotion fraction to partnership.
      • Equation: 0.10
      • Units: 1/year
    • Parameter associates.departure_rate: Fixed turnover fraction.
      • Equation: 0.05
      • Units: 1/year

  3. Module partners:

    • Ghost Variable partners.associates promotions: Cross-module reference representing incoming promotions from the associate tier.
      • Source: associates.promotions
      • Units: people/year
    • Flow partners.hires: Inflow into partnership driven by associate promotions.
      • Equation: associates_promotions
      • Units: people/year
    • Stock partners.count: Top-tier workforce stock. Initial value = 20 people.
      • Inflows: partners.hires
      • Outflows: partners.departures
      • Units: people
    • Flow partners.departures: Retirement and turnover exits.
      • Equation: count * departure_rate
      • Units: people/year
    • Parameter partners.departure_rate: Fixed annual partner departure fraction.
      • Equation: 0.05
      • Units: 1/year

Feedback Loop Structure

Feedback loop analysis identified the following balancing feedback loops governing the individual stock drains:

  • Loop 1 (B): associates.count -> associates.promotions -> associates.count (-)
  • Loop 2 (B): associates.count -> associates.departures -> associates.count (-)
  • Loop 3 (B): partners.count -> partners.departures -> partners.count (-)
  • Loop 4 (B): rookies.count -> rookies.promotions -> rookies.count (-)
  • Loop 5 (B): rookies.count -> rookies.departures -> rookies.count (-)

Structural Critique

  1. Aging Chain Pipeline: The system functions as an open-loop push pipeline where intake at the base cascades down through successive stages based purely on fractional transfer rates.
  2. First-Order Draining: Each cohort is controlled by independent first-order negative feedback loops (Loops 1 through 5) that ensure stock stability and prevent negative accumulation under non-negative initial conditions.
  3. Absence of Capacity Constraints: Upstream advancement is independent of downstream headcount constraints or organizational leverage ratios (such as target associate-to-partner ratios).

      • Path: frimbulators.count -> frimbulators.growth -> frimbulators.count
      • Polarity: Reinforcing (+)
      • Dynamic Mechanism: An increase in frimbulators.count produces a higher frimbulators.growth, which further increases frimbulators.count, generating exponential inventory growth over time.

Simultaneously, each year the stock loses 300% of whatever balacks are currently available.  Meanwhile, we begin with two hundred balacks. Model Structure

The quantitative System Dynamics model has been constructed with two dedicated modules to represent the components and their causal couplings:

1. Module whatajigs

  • Stock:
    • whatajigs.count: Initialized to 100 whatajigs.
  • Inflows:
    • whatajigs.growth: whatajigs.growth_rate * whatajigs.count (5% annual growth relative to current whatajigs count).
  • Outflows:
    • whatajigs.losses: whatajigs.loss_rate_from_balacks * whatajigs.balacks_count (Annual losses of 300% of available balacks).
  • Auxiliaries / Constants:
    • whatajigs.growth_rate: 0.05 (1/Year).
    • whatajigs.loss_rate_from_balacks: 3.0 (whatajigs/(balack*Year)).
  • Ghost Variable:
    • whatajigs.balacks count: Cross-level ghost reflecting balacks.count.

2. Module balacks

  • Stock:
    • balacks.count: Initialized to 200 balacks.
  • Inflows:
    • balacks.replenishment: balacks.replenishment_rate * balacks.whatajigs_count (Annual replenishment equal to 5% of whatajigs count).
  • Outflows:
    • balacks.losses: balacks.loss_rate * balacks.count (Annual losses equal to 3% of current balacks count).
  • Auxiliaries / Constants:
    • balacks.replenishment_rate: 0.05 (balacks/(whatajig*Year)).
    • balacks.loss_rate: 0.03 (1/Year).
  • Ghost Variable:
    • balacks.whatajigs count: Cross-level ghost reflecting whatajigs.count.

Feedback Loop Analysis

Based on the feedback loop analysis of the system, the model contains three structural feedback loops:

  1. Loop 1 (L1, Balancing / -): Balacks Self-Regulation

    • Path: balacks.count -> (+) balacks.losses -> (-) balacks.count
    • Mechanism: A first-order balancing feedback loop where higher accumulated balacks increase fractional annual losses (at 3%/year), stabilizing the stock.

  2. Loop 2 (L2, Balancing / -): Inter-Module Coupling Loop

    • Path: balacks.count -> (+) whatajigs.balacks count -> (+) whatajigs.losses -> (-) whatajigs.count -> (+) balacks.whatajigs count -> (+) balacks.replenishment -> (+) balacks.count
    • Mechanism: A multi-stock negative feedback loop linking both modules across ghost boundaries. A higher count of balacks accelerates whatajigs losses; as whatajigs decline, balacks replenishment is constrained, ultimately reducing the balacks count.

  3. Loop 3 (L3, Reinforcing / +): Whatajigs Autonomous Growth

    • Path: whatajigs.count -> (+) whatajigs.growth -> (+) whatajigs.count
    • Mechanism: A first-order reinforcing growth loop where existing whatajigs generate 5% annual growth relative to their current inventory size.

Simultaneously, each day the stock experiences losses of 20% of its current amount.  Meanwhile, we have on hand ninety auspongs. Model Architecture and Causal Structure

A modular System Dynamics model has been constructed to capture all causal relationships and inventory dynamics specified in the background information.

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MODULE: dominitoxings                                                                 |
|   [replenishment_rate: 12] ---> (replenishment) ---> [dominitoxings.count] (Init: 45) |
|                                                              |     |                  |

|   <povals.dominitoxings count> (Ghost)                                                |
|            |                                                                          |
|            v                                                                          |
|   [enhancement_fraction: 0.30] -> (enhancement) ----> [povals.count] (Init: 35)      |

|   [loss_fraction: 0.20] ------------------------------------> (losses) <-------------+

|            |                                                                          |
|            v                                                                          |
|   [addition_fraction: 0.20] ----> (additions) ------> [auspongs.count] (Init: 90)     |
|                                                              |                        |
|   [diminishing_rate: 12] ---------------------------> (diminishment)                  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Module Specifications

1. Module dominitoxings

  • Stock: dominitoxings.count
    • Initial Value: 45
    • Units: dominitoxings
    • Inflows: dominitoxings.replenishment
    • Outflows: dominitoxings.losses
    • Documentation: Current inventory count of dominitoxings.
  • Auxiliary: dominitoxings.replenishment_rate
    • Equation: 12
    • Units: dominitoxings/day
    • Documentation: Constant daily replenishment rate.
  • Flow (Inflow): dominitoxings.replenishment
    • Equation: replenishment_rate
    • Units: dominitoxings/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Inflow replenishing dominitoxings daily.
  • Auxiliary: dominitoxings.loss_fraction
    • Equation: 0.30
    • Units: 1/day
    • Documentation: Fractional loss rate per day (30%).
  • Flow (Outflow): dominitoxings.losses
    • Equation: count * loss_fraction
    • Units: dominitoxings/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Daily losses draining the dominitoxings stock.

2. Module povals

  • Stock: povals.count
    • Initial Value: 35
    • Units: povals
    • Inflows: povals.enhancement
    • Outflows: povals.losses
    • Documentation: Current inventory count of povals.
  • Ghost Variable: povals.dominitoxings count
    • Cross-Level Source: dominitoxings.count
    • Units: dominitoxings
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost variable providing the dominitoxings inventory count to the povals module.
  • Auxiliary: povals.enhancement_fraction
    • Equation: 0.30
    • Units: povals/(dominitoxings*day)
    • Documentation: Daily enhancement rate per unit of dominitoxings (30%).
  • Flow (Inflow): povals.enhancement
    • Equation: dominitoxings_count * enhancement_fraction
    • Units: povals/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Daily additions to povals driven by the dominitoxings inventory.
  • Auxiliary: povals.loss_fraction
    • Equation: 0.20
    • Units: 1/day
    • Documentation: Fractional loss rate per day (20%).
  • Flow (Outflow): povals.losses
    • Equation: count * loss_fraction
    • Units: povals/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Daily losses draining the povals stock.

3. Module auspongs

  • Stock: auspongs.count
    • Initial Value: 90
    • Units: auspongs
    • Inflows: auspongs.additions
    • Outflows: auspongs.diminishment
    • Documentation: Current inventory count of auspongs.
  • Ghost Variable: auspongs.povals count
    • Cross-Level Source: povals.count
    • Units: povals
    • Documentation: Cross-module ghost variable providing the povals inventory count to the auspongs module.
  • Auxiliary: auspongs.addition_fraction
    • Equation: 0.20
    • Units: auspongs/(povals*day)
    • Documentation: Daily addition rate per unit of povals (20%).
  • Flow (Inflow): auspongs.additions
    • Equation: povals_count * addition_fraction
    • Units: auspongs/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Daily additions to auspongs driven by the povals inventory.
  • Auxiliary: auspongs.diminishing_rate
    • Equation: 12
    • Units: auspongs/day
    • Documentation: Constant daily diminishing rate.
  • Flow (Outflow): auspongs.diminishment
    • Equation: diminishing_rate
    • Units: auspongs/day
    • Uniflow: true
    • Documentation: Constant daily outflow diminishing the auspongs stock.

Causal Relationship Network

  1. dominitoxings.replenishment_rate -> dominitoxings.replenishment (+): Higher replenishment rate increases the replenishment inflow.
  2. dominitoxings.replenishment -> dominitoxings.count (+): Replenishment inflow accumulates into the dominitoxings inventory.
  3. dominitoxings.count -> dominitoxings.losses (+): Higher stock level causes higher absolute fractional losses.
  4. dominitoxings.loss_fraction -> dominitoxings.losses (+): Higher loss fraction increases the rate of loss.
  5. dominitoxings.losses -> dominitoxings.count (-): Losses reduce the dominitoxings stock.
  6. povals.dominitoxings count -> povals.enhancement (+): Greater dominitoxings inventory drives higher enhancement additions to povals.
  7. povals.enhancement_fraction -> povals.enhancement (+): Higher enhancement fraction increases daily enhancement flow.
  8. povals.enhancement -> povals.count (+): Enhancement flow accumulates into the povals stock.
  9. povals.count -> povals.losses (+): Larger povals inventory yields higher absolute losses.
  10. povals.loss_fraction -> povals.losses (+): Higher loss fraction increases povals outflow.
  11. povals.losses -> povals.count (-): Losses reduce the povals inventory.
  12. auspongs.povals count -> auspongs.additions (+): Greater povals inventory drives higher additions to auspongs.
  13. auspongs.addition_fraction -> auspongs.additions (+): Higher addition fraction increases additions inflow.
  14. auspongs.additions -> auspongs.count (+): Additions accumulate directly into the auspongs inventory.
  15. auspongs.diminishing_rate -> auspongs.diminishment (+): Higher diminishing rate directly sets higher diminishment outflow.
  16. auspongs.diminishment -> auspongs.count (-): Diminishment reduces the auspongs inventory.

Feedback Loop Structure (from Engine Analysis)

  • Loop L1 (Balancing - Dominitoxings Adjustment):
    • Cycle: dominitoxings.count -> dominitoxings.losses -> dominitoxings.count
    • Mechanism: First-order negative feedback regulating dominitoxings.count from its initial value of 45 toward its dynamic equilibrium of 40 (where replenishment of 12 units/day equals losses of 40 * 0.30 = 12 units/day).
  • Loop L2 (Balancing - Povals Adjustment):
    • Cycle: povals.count -> povals.losses -> povals.count
    • Mechanism: First-order negative feedback regulating povals.count from its initial value of 35 toward an equilibrium of 60 (as dominitoxings settles at 40, enhancement settles at 12 units/day, balancing losses of 60 * 0.20 = 12 units/day).
  • Auspongs Subsystem Dynamics:
    • Driven in an open-loop cascade by the upstream povals.count. As povals rise toward 60, additions increase from 7 units/day toward 12 units/day, balancing the constant diminishment outflow of 12 units/day and stabilizing the stock.

Simulation Parameters

  • Start Time: 0
  • Stop Time: 50
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25
  • Time Units: Days
  • Integration Method: Euler

Model Structure Overview

A modular Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) simulation model has been constructed to represent the causal structure described in the background information. The model is structured into four dedicated modules: ocs, proptimatires, priaries, and houtals.

Module Details

1. Module: ocs

  • Stock:
    • ocs.count: Initial value = 25 ocs.
    • Inflows: ocs.inflow
    • Outflows: ocs.outflow
  • Flows:
    • ocs.inflow: Additions to ocs inventory. Equation: ocs.proptimatires_fraction * ocs.proptimatires_count (Units: ocs/Weeks).
    • ocs.outflow: Weekly loss from ocs inventory. Equation: ocs.decrease_rate (Units: ocs/Weeks).
  • Variables & Parameters:
    • ocs.proptimatires count: Cross-level ghost variable referencing proptimatires.count (Units: proptimatires).
    • ocs.proptimatires_fraction: Fractional rate of proptimatires contributing to ocs = 0.15 (Units: 1/Weeks).
    • ocs.decrease_rate: Constant weekly decrease rate = 3 (Units: ocs/Weeks).

2. Module: proptimatires

  • Stock:
    • proptimatires.count: Initial value = 40 proptimatires.
    • Inflows: proptimatires.inflow
    • Outflows: proptimatires.outflow
  • Flows:
    • proptimatires.inflow: Weekly additions. Equation: proptimatires.addition_rate (Units: proptimatires/Weeks).
    • proptimatires.outflow: Fractional reduction. Equation: proptimatires.count * proptimatires.reduction_fraction (Units: proptimatires/Weeks).
  • Variables & Parameters:
    • proptimatires.addition_rate: Constant weekly addition rate = 5 (Units: proptimatires/Weeks).
    • proptimatires.reduction_fraction: Weekly reduction fraction = 0.25 (Units: 1/Weeks).

3. Module: priaries

  • Stock:
    • priaries.count: Initial value = 80 priaries.
    • Inflows: priaries.inflow
    • Outflows: priaries.outflow
  • Flows:
    • priaries.inflow: Additions driven by proptimatires. Equation: priaries.proptimatires_fraction * priaries.proptimatires_count (Units: priaries/Weeks).
    • priaries.outflow: Losses driven by available houtals. Equation: priaries.loss_fraction * priaries.houtals_count (Units: priaries/Weeks).
  • Variables & Parameters:
    • priaries.proptimatires count: Cross-level ghost variable referencing proptimatires.count (Units: proptimatires).
    • priaries.proptimatires_fraction: Fractional rate of proptimatires contributing to priaries = 0.10 (Units: 1/Weeks).
    • priaries.houtals count: Cross-level ghost variable referencing houtals.count (Units: houtals).
    • priaries.loss_fraction: Fractional loss factor per available houtal = 0.05 (Units: 1/Weeks).

4. Module: houtals

  • Stock:
    • houtals.count: Initial value = 60 houtals.
    • Inflows: houtals.inflow
    • Outflows: houtals.outflow
  • Flows:
    • houtals.inflow: Weekly additions. Equation: houtals.addition_rate (Units: houtals/Weeks).
    • houtals.outflow: Fractional diminishing rate. Equation: houtals.count * houtals.diminishing_fraction (Units: houtals/Weeks).
  • Variables & Parameters:
    • houtals.addition_rate: Constant weekly addition rate = 7 (Units: houtals/Weeks).
    • houtals.diminishing_fraction: Weekly diminishing fraction = 0.08 (Units: 1/Weeks).

Simulation Specifications

  • Start Time: 0
  • Stop Time: 50
  • Time Step (dt): 0.25
  • Time Units: Weeks
  • Integration Method: Euler

A modular Stock Flow Diagram (SFD) model has been constructed to represent all entities, stocks, flows, and causal interactions specified in the background information.

Model Architecture and Modular Structure

The model is partitioned into four distinct modules corresponding to each object:

  1. Module outrances

    • Stock outrances.count: Represents the total accumulation of outrances on hand.
      • Initial Value: 150 outrances
      • Inflows: outrances.replenishment
      • Outflows: outrances.loss, outrances.outgoing
    • Variable outrances.replenishment_rate: Constant rate of 20 outrances/hour.
    • Flow outrances.replenishment: Inflow set by outrances.replenishment_rate (20 outrances/hour).
    • Variable outrances.loss_fraction: Fractional loss factor of 0.40 (1/hour).
    • Flow outrances.loss: Outflow defined by outrances.count * outrances.loss_fraction (40% of current stock per hour).
    • Variable outrances.outgoing_fraction: Fractional outgoing factor of 0.10 (1/hour).
    • Flow outrances.outgoing: Outflow defined by outrances.count * outrances.outgoing_fraction (10% of current stock per hour).

  2. Module illigents

    • Stock illigents.count: Represents the total accumulation of illigents on hand.
      • Initial Value: 30 illigents
      • Inflows: illigents.additions
      • Outflows: illigents.diminishment
    • Ghost Variable illigents.outrances count: Cross-module ghost referencing outrances.count.
    • Variable illigents.addition_fraction: Fractional addition coefficient of 0.40 (1/hour).
    • Flow illigents.additions: Inflow defined by illigents.outrances_count * illigents.addition_fraction (40% of outrances count per hour).
    • Variable illigents.diminishment_rate: Constant diminishment rate of 5 illigents/hour.
    • Flow illigents.diminishment: Outflow defined by illigents.diminishment_rate (5 illigents/hour).

  3. Module yelbs

    • Stock yelbs.count: Represents the total accumulation of yelbs on hand.
      • Initial Value: 65 yelbs
      • Inflows: yelbs.enhancement
      • Outflows: yelbs.depletion
    • Ghost Variable yelbs.outrances count: Cross-module ghost referencing outrances.count.
    • Variable yelbs.enhancement_fraction: Fractional enhancement coefficient of 0.10 (1/hour).
    • Flow yelbs.enhancement: Inflow defined by yelbs.outrances_count * yelbs.enhancement_fraction (10% of outrances count per hour).
    • Ghost Variable yelbs.trazes count: Cross-module ghost referencing trazes.count.
    • Variable yelbs.depletion_fraction: Fractional depletion coefficient of 0.12 (1/hour).
    • Flow yelbs.depletion: Outflow defined by yelbs.trazes_count * yelbs.depletion_fraction (12% of available trazes per hour).

  4. Module trazes

    • Stock trazes.count: Represents the total accumulation of trazes on hand.
      • Initial Value: 85 trazes
      • Inflows: trazes.incoming
      • Outflows: trazes.decrease
    • Variable trazes.incoming_rate: Constant incoming rate of 15 trazes/hour.
    • Flow trazes.incoming: Inflow defined by trazes.incoming_rate (15 trazes/hour).
    • Variable trazes.decrease_fraction: Fractional decrease factor of 0.18 (1/hour).
    • Flow trazes.decrease: Outflow defined by trazes.count * trazes.decrease_fraction (18% of current stock per hour).

Summary of Causal Relationships

  • outrances.replenishment_rate (+) -> outrances.replenishment (+) -> outrances.count
  • outrances.count (+) -> outrances.loss (-) -> outrances.count
  • outrances.loss_fraction (+) -> outrances.loss
  • outrances.count (+) -> outrances.outgoing (-) -> outrances.count
  • outrances.outgoing_fraction (+) -> outrances.outgoing
  • outrances.count -> illigents.outrances count (+) -> illigents.additions (+) -> illigents.count

  • illigents.diminishment_rate (+) -> illigents.diminishment (-) -> illigents.count
  • outrances.count -> yelbs.outrances count (+) -> yelbs.enhancement (+) -> yelbs.count
  • yelbs.enhancement_fraction (+) -> yelbs.enhancement
  • trazes.count -> yelbs.trazes count (+) -> yelbs.depletion (-) -> yelbs.count
  • yelbs.depletion_fraction (+) -> yelbs.depletion
  • trazes.incoming_rate (+) -> trazes.incoming (+) -> trazes.count
  • trazes.count (+) -> trazes.decrease (-) -> trazes.count

Causal Relationship Matrix

  1. Whatajigs Subsystem:

    • whatajigs.count -> whatajigs.growth (+)
    • whatajigs.growth_fraction -> whatajigs.growth (+)
    • whatajigs.growth -> whatajigs.count (+)
    • whatajigs.constant_outgoing_rate -> whatajigs.outgoing (+)
    • whatajigs.outgoing -> whatajigs.count (-)

  2. Balacks Subsystem & Inter-Module Coupling:

    • whatajigs.count -> balacks.whatajigs count (+)
    • balacks.whatajigs count -> balacks.gain (+)
    • balacks.gain_fraction -> balacks.gain (+)
    • balacks.gain -> balacks.count (+)
    • balacks.count -> balacks.diminishment (+)
    • balacks.loss_fraction -> balacks.diminishment (+)
    • balacks.diminishment -> balacks.count (-)

  3. Whoziewhats Subsystem & Inter-Module Coupling:

    • balacks.count -> whoziewhats.balacks count (+)
    • whoziewhats.balacks count -> whoziewhats.increase (+)
    • whoziewhats.increase_fraction -> whoziewhats.increase (+)
    • whoziewhats.increase -> whoziewhats.count (+)
    • whoziewhats.count -> whoziewhats.losses (+)
    • whoziewhats.loss_fraction -> whoziewhats.losses (+)
    • whoziewhats.losses -> whoziewhats.count (-)

  4. Funkados & Maxabizers Cross-Coupled Subsystem:

    • whoziewhats.count -> funkados.whoziewhats count (+)
    • funkados.whoziewhats count -> funkados.gain (+)
    • funkados.gain_fraction -> funkados.gain (+)
    • funkados.gain -> funkados.count (+)
    • maxabizers.count -> funkados.maxabizers count (+)
    • funkados.maxabizers count -> funkados.losses (+)
    • funkados.loss_fraction -> funkados.losses (+)
    • funkados.losses -> funkados.count (-)
    • funkados.count -> maxabizers.funkados count (+)
    • maxabizers.funkados count -> maxabizers.replenishment (+)
    • maxabizers.replenishment_fraction -> maxabizers.replenishment (+)
    • maxabizers.replenishment -> maxabizers.count (+)
    • whoziewhats.count -> maxabizers.whoziewhats count (+)
    • maxabizers.whoziewhats count -> maxabizers.decrease (+)
    • maxabizers.decrease_fraction -> maxabizers.decrease (+)
    • maxabizers.decrease -> maxabizers.count (-)

Feedback Loop Structure

Feedback loop analysis identified the following primary feedback loops active across the simulation:

  • Loop L3 (Reinforcing): whatajigs.count -> whatajigs.growth -> whatajigs.count
    • Captures the endogenous compound growth of whatajigs inventory driving upstream material availability.
  • Loop L1 (Balancing): balacks.count -> balacks.diminishment -> balacks.count
    • Provides first-order negative feedback regulating the balacks inventory relative to its outflow rate.
  • Loop L4 (Balancing): whoziewhats.count -> whoziewhats.losses -> whoziewhats.count
    • Regulates whoziewhats stock level through internal loss dynamics.
  • Loop L2 (Balancing): funkados.count -> maxabizers.funkados count -> maxabizers.replenishment -> maxabizers.count -> funkados.maxabizers count -> funkados.losses -> funkados.count
    • A two-stock cross-module balancing loop coupling funkados and maxabizers: increases in funkados replenish maxabizers, which subsequently elevates the loss rate of funkados, stabilizing the downstream subsystem.
